title: RVBH Mental Health Art Contest; deadline April 26
description: RiverValley Behavioral Health is celebrating its 4th Annual Youth Mental Health Art Contest. The event encourages youth in our communities to express messages of hope and raise awareness about mental…
content: RiverValley Behavioral Health is celebrating its 4th Annual Youth Mental Health Art Contest. The event encourages youth in our communities to express messages of hope and raise awareness about mental health through artistic expression, centered around the theme, 'Be Kind to Your Mind. The contest began in May 2021 during the pandemic to support mental health awareness among youth. Throughout the last three years, RVBH has received more than 1,000 art submissions and has awarded more than $10,000 worth of scholarship funds and donations throughout our school districts and local youth organizations. 'The Youth Mental Health Art Contest serves as a beacon of hope, reminding our youth of the vital importance of mental health. Through artistic expression, we aim to empower them and foster a sense of unity and hope. The ripple affect The ripple effect of this contest extends far beyond the strokes of a paintbrush or the lines of a poem; it permeates the fabric of our communities, weaving a tapestry of compassion, empathy, and solidarity,' said Dr. Wanda Figueroa-Peralta, RVBH President & CEO. 'We extend our gratitude to our schools and youth organizations for their unwavering support of this event. Together, we strive to foster self-expression and convey a message of hope among the youth, united in our shared commitment to their growth and well-being.' Students in grades K-College throughout our seven-county region in Kentucky (Daviess, Hancock, Henderson, McLean, Ohio, Union, and Webster counties) are invited to create and submit a visual art piece (drawing, painting, sculpture, poem, etc.) to share a message of support with the theme, 'Be Kind to Your Mind.' Scholarships A $500 scholarship will be awarded to the project of the year winner in each division, K-4; 5-8; 9-12; and college (ages 18-24), with a matching contribution awarded to the school or organization chosen by the winners. The organization with the most entries will be named, 'Mental Health Partner of the Year,' with an award of $1,000. Submission Deadline Entries must include a completed submission form and be postmarked or received by April 26, 2024. Finalists will be announced in May during Mental Health Awareness Month and invited to attend an awards ceremony in June. 'We are continually impressed with the insight students in our communities showcase through their artwork. We had over 600 entries last year and I'm confident the bar will be raised even higher this year,' said Brooke Arnold, Director of the RVBH Regional Prevention Center. 'It is always a joy to see such talent recognized in these young people.' RVBH is also accepting nominations for the Dianne McFarling Memorial Award, which will be announced during the awards ceremony. Nominations accepted through April 26, 2024 The Dianne McFarling Memorial Award commemorates the work of the late Dianne McFarling, who served as the Senior Director of RiverValley's Regional Prevention Center for 21 years. It is awarded to an organization, business, nonprofit, charity, school, group or individual in our region that has demonstrated a commitment to improving mental health in our communities. To learn more, make a nomination, or download the art submission form, visit www.rvbh.com/artcontest.

title: Hancock Elementary Schools – Best at Implementing Reading Strategies
description: IMSE Co-Founder Jeanne Jeup telling HC E
content: IMSE Co-Founder Jeanne Jeup telling HC Elementary Teachers what a wonderful job they're doing. She and IMSE Academics Director Kimberly Collins visited NHES and SHES last Wednesday. Seen in background are SHES Principal Jennifer Howe and HC Schools Superintendent Robby Asberry. Hancock County Schools Assistant Superintendent Robin Poynter said she felt that the visit received from the IMSE Co-Founder last week helped to affirm to the teachers that they are on the 'right track with classroom rigor' to teach students how to read. IMSE (Institute for Multi-Sensory Education) Co-Founder Jeanne Jeup and IMSE Director of Academics & Instructor Kimberly Collins visited and observed at North and South Hancock Elementary Schools' classrooms. They have visited thousands of classrooms and had nothing but great things to say about the teachers and administration. They said they were very impressed with how the curriculum is being implemented in both schools. 'Our district is one-of-a-kind in the state of Kentucky,' Poynter said, 'where our students are fortunate enough to have each of their teachers trained and supported by a district Literacy Coach. The fact that we have had over 400 visitors from all across the state in the past 2 years and their feedback of how our district is the best they have ever seen, is a testament to all of their hard work aligning instruction Pre-K-12th grade. Our next steps in the district are to support our Grades 3 through Grades 10 with the methodology of Morphology which will help our students improve reading comprehension, vocabulary meaning and spelling skills.' All of the teachers and most of the teaching assistants have been trained through IMSE the Science of Reading, which uses an Orton-Gillingham (OG) approach in teaching students how to read. After classroom walkthroughs at both elementary schools, a reception was held at SHES in the afternoon on Wednesday, March 20th, for teachers to meet Jeup and Collins personally. HUGE Growth Jeup, who since '96 has trained hundreds of thousands of educators worldwide, said to everyone attending, 'Thank you for letting us come into your classrooms and see the growth you've made; It's HUGE growth. And, what an impact you're making on those kiddos! It's so evident that you're using it in your classrooms because those routines are succinct. Those kids know what to do; there's no lag time. Congratulations! Be proud of yourselves and give yourselves a pat on the back.' Classrooms Like Well-Oiled Machines Collins shared very positive feedback as well saying, 'You are an incredibly strong group of educators. Your classrooms were like well-oiled machines. Your children were responsive. You can tell that your heart is in what you do and you're making great progress with your kids. It was so much a pleasure to be here and to see you today. I can't say enough good things about what we saw. Kudos to all of you. Every classroom we were in was super impressive.' Poynter thanked the teachers saying, 'I appreciate everything you're doing for our kids. The middle school and high school are getting on board as well. I think it's a huge step. The strategies of how to implement the instruction, I thank you all for. At one time, we were only going to include 3rd-8th until the high school visited the elementary schools last week, and now we've added 9th and 10th. The consistency and delivery of instruction you've been giving your students every day can't be measured except for the benefit of the students when they graduate.' SHES Principal Jennifer Howe echoed that by saying that every one of the administrators that have visited have had tears in their eyes by the end of the day after visiting classrooms in Hancock County and seeing the IMSE curriculum being implemented seamlessly, and how the students are engaged and excelling in it. Poynter added, 'Great things are coming in Hancock County. I can't wait to see how well the students are going to be doing after 12 years of this rigor. Sustainability is very important to us as well so we've got Briana Pulliam (District Literacy Coach/Interventionist) taking a crack at those. We've also got a couple doing practicum, and someone doing Morphology at NHES and you're doing Morphology here (at SHES), so we're trying to put things in place for you so you'll have the things that you need to thrive.' By Jennifer Wimmer

title: Hwy 60 Widening to Resume April 3rd – Expect Traffic Delays & Lane Closures April 3rd-September 30th
description: Yager Materials in Owensboro was contracted by the KY Transportation Cabinet to widen Hwy 60 from just east of the entrance at Vastwood Park
content: Yager Materials in Owensboro was contracted by the KY Transportation Cabinet to widen Hwy 60 from just east of the entrance at Vastwood Park to 1957, and work started in mid-April of last year. Traffic returned to a 4-lane and resumed normal patterns beginning Thursday, November 9th, 2023 due to weather and temperature variances, and starting on Wednesday night, April 3rd, Hwy 60 will go back to a 2-lane and work will resume. (*Signage in some areas is now reporting Friday, April 5th for the start date.) Work will occur daily from Wednesday, April 3rd through Monday, September 30th, between 7 a.m. and 5 p.m. The project will stretch from milepost 4.5 at John Pate Road to milepost 9.6 at KY 3101. Both westbound lanes will be closed until the work is completed. The passing lane on the eastbound side will be used for westbound traffic. Anticipate Delays/Adhere to Posted Signage KYTC Highway District 2 advises motorists to plan their routes accordingly, anticipate delays and adhere to all posted signage and instructions within the work zone. The work will involve removal and repairing of existing roadway, widening measures to accommodate increased traffic flow, and ensuring safer travel conditions. Traffic Advisories To receive traffic advisories and alerts for KYTC Highway District 2 counties via email, go to: https://public.govdelievery.com/accounts/KYTC/signup/13668. Click on the District 2 counties you regularly drive through or on any of the specialty corridors you travel. Confirm your subscription request when you receive the corresponding email message after signing up. The KYTC website is: https://transportation.ky.gov. By Jennifer Wimmer

title: Hornets win huge meet at HCHS
description: Cooper Jones long jumps last week at HCHS. The sophomore won the event and led the Hornets with 23 points during a track meet victory for Hancock County. Hancock County High School hosted their…
content: Cooper Jones long jumps last week at HCHS. The sophomore won the event and led the Hornets with 23 points during a track meet victory for Hancock County. Hancock County High School hosted their largest track meet in history with seven schools competing on Tuesday, March 26. The Hornet boys team took first place. 'Our boys did well across the board. We would not be undefeated on our new track if we didn't have solid boys in every event,' HCHS coach Wes Meserve said. 'Cooper was the top individual point earner at the meet with 23 points. We had several season and career personal best performances across all events.' Ben Baker won the 100 meter dash against 40 athletes with a time of 11.30 seconds. title: Ham Fundraiser brings in nearly $6000 for Youth Baseball Fields
description: The Ham Fundraiser raised close to $6K. The money raised will go to maintenance of the Hancock County Youth Baseball fields at Vastwood Park.
content: The Ham Fundraiser on Friday, March 29th raised close to $6K. The money raised will go to maintenance of the Hancock County Youth Baseball fields at Vastwood Park. Over 250 hams were sold, at $40 each. Hancock County Youth Baseball Board members organized the fundraiser. They are: League President Nathan Maxwell, Wade Gaynor, Brodie Cox, Joe Hager, Trey Anderson and B.J. Burton. Brodie used his own sorghum as part of the recipe for the seasoning on the hams and it made them turn out very delicious, people said. Some locals donated their smoker for the day, and there were 10 to 15 people smoking hams all day long. Field Packing, in Owensboro, gave the organizers a really good deal on the hams, Wade Gaynor said. Along with the help of Hancock County Fiscal Court, the HC Youth Baseball Board was able to install a brand new fence on the little league field (front field). Barry Griffin helped with the playing surface as well. The Board has painted, bought new bases & home plate, and are hoping to start on the back field next year (the t-ball diamond). The season starts April 13th, and this year there are: 2 teams in major, 4 teams in minor, and 14 teams in rookie and t-ball. By Jennifer Wimmer

title: Healthy Habits: Baking Soda
description: Baking soda, or sodium bicarbonate, is inexpensive and has so many uses – not just as a household cleaner though. For instance, because it is anti-fungal, oncologists have reported that it can shrink…
content: Baking soda, or sodium bicarbonate, is inexpensive and has so many uses – not just as a household cleaner though. For instance, because it is anti-fungal, oncologists have reported that it can shrink cancerous tumors within days. That's because there is a connection between fungal infection and growing cancers. Internal vs. External When you're taking baking soda mixed with filtered water internally as a home remedy for heartburn/acid reflux, migraine headaches or any of its other amazing cures, it is important to use an organic, naturally made brand such as Frontier or Bob's Red Mill. While generic brands and even the trusted Arm & Hammer is great and cheap for cleaning and refreshing all the rooms in your home, as well as laundry and oodles of other household cleaning hacks, those brands typically do not mine the sodium bicarbonate naturally. It is not just mined with a chemical reaction process but is also then usually heated and treated before being boxed, rendering it less potent and less natural. If you are ingesting it or applying it topically in any way, then reach for the natural stuff and save your Great Value brand for freshening up the fridge. Detox Brands like Frontier Co-op mine the sodium bicarbonate directly from the ground, in its natural state. Choose these for when you're, for instance, mixing a teaspoon or less of baking soda with filtered water and drinking first thing in the morning for an excellent detox from parasites, heavy metals and other toxins that you may have absorbed from the environment around you – the air, your drinking water, additives in foods/drinks, etc. Make yourself a detox bath to help pull toxins out. To a full bath, add a half cup of baking soda, several drops of detoxing essential oils such as lavender, and a half cup of Celtic sea salt or other natural sea salt. The same ingredients can be used for a detoxing foot soak. Baking soda can also be used as a natural hair rinse and as an exfoliative. Use the natural brands for these purposes, and for swishing with as well. Swishing with a small amount of baking soda mixed in filtered water after brushing your teeth is a great extra step to sanitize the gums and teeth and prevent cavities. Follow that with swishing a small amount of hydrogen peroxide diluted with filtered water (swish and spit out). Brushing with baking soda is a great teeth-whitening method also. Here is a list of just some of baking soda's many possible health perks: boosts the immune system, alkalizes/balances pH, reduces ulcer pain, can cure ulcers, antibacterial, antifungal, anti-parasitic, anti-cancer, relieves sunburn, soothes itchy skin/treats mosquito bites & poison ivy (add filtered water and make a paste to apply), relieves digestive challenges, alleviates urinary tract infections (UTI), promotes kidney health, treats canker sores, helps remove splinters, reduces calluses, can help increase athletic performance/boosts stamina, relieves cough & other cold symptoms, clears acne, a natural deodorant, fights skin infections, eases rheumatic pains and is a powerful ingredient for sitz baths. Counterindications Baking soda is very high in sodium and ingesting a large amount is not recommended. Make sure you do your research and/or talk with your doctor first before taking baking soda mixed with water as a detox, for example. Abide by the recommended dosage for your age, weight and height. title: Crescent Paper Tube Plant Employees take steps to Unionize
description: The twenty production and maintenance employees at Crescent Paper Tube in Lewisport voted last week to unionize. The majority (16 employees) voted to unionize, with 4 who were opposed. Crescent Paper…
content: The twenty production and maintenance employees at Crescent Paper Tube in Lewisport voted last week to unionize. The majority (16 employees) voted to unionize, with 4 who were opposed. Crescent Paper Tube Company, Inc. is one of the thriving businesses located in Lewisport Industrial Park, and a leading manufacturer in the American paper tube industry. The company began in 1919 and is headquartered in Florence, Kentucky. Management at the Lewisport location is not providing comments at this time concerning their production & maintenance employees voting to unionize. A petition was filed on February 28th by United Steel Workers Organizer Sam Elliott, who volunteered to run the campaign. The employees who want to unionize are dissatisfied with their wages, benefits and insurance they're required to have with extremely high premiums, he said. All 20 production & maintenance employees voted on Wednesday, March 27th. 'The workers called me and wanted to organize,' Sam said. 'They first reached out to the local Union Hall (USW Local Union # 9443) in Lewisport. The staff representative that services Aleris (Commonwealth Rolled Products) and Domtar is Richard Haas. They contacted him and he called me. I'm a retired steel worker organizer but they asked me if I would run this campaign for them and I told them I would. I filed a petition to organize an election for them. From the time I filed the petition to the election, the company hired several union busters (union busting law firms) to come into the plant and try to convince workers that it would not be in their best interest to unionize. They were dishonest with the workers; that's typical in a union campaign.' Sam said the next step is gathering information from the company about their policies, wages and benefits, etc. 'Once the company sends us that information then we'll reach out to the company and get some dates to sit down and negotiate a contract,' he said. 'The company and the union both have 7 days to file objections to the election with the Labor Board. I don't expect that will happen. Certainly the union is not going to be filing an objection because we won the election, and we won by such a margin that I doubt that the company would object to anything. Plus, there was no objectionable conduct that was done by the union. After the 7 days, we will send the company an information request asking them about the hiring dates of all their employees, what their policies are now, all about their insurance premiums and their benefits that they receive, their wages, etc. Then we'll meet with the employees again and prepare a contract proposal, and we'll notify the company that we're ready to meet. The company will give us some dates and we'll give them some dates. Probably within a month or so we'll sit down for our first bargain session with the company and go from there. The steel workers are not interested in letting the company drag this out for a lengthy period of time. We're going to be fair and we expect the company to be fair as well and to move this along as quickly as possible. We have to look to see what they have first, to see what all of their benefits are, etc. Then we'll look at other people in that industry and see how it compares and base our proposal on like industries. It is a paper company and we have Domtar in Hawesville and in Owensboro. The USW represent the majority of all paper plants in America. We have a lot of things that we can look at to see how we base our proposal.' The law requires the company and the union to bargain in good faith. That means that the company and the union both have to make proposals and they have to try to reach an agreement on those proposals. 'This being a first contract, it's going to be covering everything from A to Z,' he added. 'There's a lot of work to do before we even meet with the company. It depends on how busy the people are that are negotiating the contract. It might be me; I don't know yet. I haven't talked to my director (District 8 USW Director Larry Ray). Typically, we'll probably be ready to sit down and start bargaining sometime in April.' Sam has been an organizer since 1995 and has been semi-retired since 2015. District 8 covers 4 states: Maryland, West Virginia, Virginia and Kentucky. The 20 Crescent Paper Tube employees will be amalgamated with Local USW 9443, he said, which represents 1,200 workers in Hancock County at Commonwealth Rolled Products and Domtar. The USW has 850K members in the U.S., Canada and the Caribbean. It is the largest private-sector union in North America. By Jennfier Wimmer

title: New Hawesville Chief of Police; New SRO Assignments at HC Schools
description: B.J. B
content:
B.J. Burton, seen here with his wife, Janna, and their son, Easton, was sworn-in as Hawesville Chief of Police by Hawesville City Councilman Danny Doyle Tuesday during the Hawesville City Council Meeting. In background are Hawesville Mayor Robbie McCormick and council members.
Hancock County Sheriff Dale Bozarth has hired former Hawesville Chief of Police Cody Axton. Cody was sworn-in by Judge-Executive Johnny 'Chic' Roberts for the position of Deputy Sheriff in late March. Deputy B.J. Burton has been sworn-in as the new Hawesville Chief of Police.
Hawesville Mayor Robbie McCormick said at the Hawesville Council Meeting on Tuesday that Burton, 'brings a lot of experience, and knows a lot of people in town. He and Cody have gotten together and he's willing to follow the lead that Cody has initiated with the small businesses and checking their buildings to make sure they're safe. He brings new ideas to the table, which is going to benefit us also.'
Bozarth also hired Cory Axton, Cody's twin brother and former Owensboro Police Dept. Deputy. Cory will be assigned to patrol. Cody and Cory both began their shifts on April 1st.
New SRO Assignments at HC Schools Deputy Sheriff Cody Axton will now be serving as School Resource Officer (SRO) at South Hancock Elementary School. Deputy Mark Powers has switched over from serving as SRO at South Hancock Elementary to serving as SRO at Hancock County High School. Deputy Butch Garst, previous SRO at HCMS/HCHS Campus, is no longer serving as SRO.
HC Schools Superintendent Robby Asberry said Mitch Brown will be the new SRO at Hancock County Middle School, and Deputy Frank Howard, previous North Hancock Elementary SRO, is no longer serving as SRO.
On February 26th, John Garner, former Lewisport Chief of Police and Dist.1 Magistrate, was sworn-in as the new SRO for North Hancock Elementary. Garner was also recognized and introduced to the board members at the Hancock County Board of Education meeting in February.

title: Lady Hornets beat Catholic to win All 'A' region title!
description: The HCHS Lady Hornets softball team poses with the championship trophy after winning the All 'A' Classic 3rd Region Tournament at Whitesville Tuesday. Pictured in the front row are: Layni Roberts,…
content:
The HCHS Lady Hornets softball team poses with the championship trophy after winning the All 'A' Classic 3rd Region Tournament at Whitesville Tuesday. Pictured in the front row are: Layni Roberts, Ella House, Kylie Westerfield, Emmalynn Higdon, Lily Roberts, Baylee Estes, Ava Riggs and Jordyn Waltrip. Standing: head coach Dwayne Wroe, coach Todd Keown, Ryleigh French, Ansley House, Madyson Higdon, Bella Bryant, Carolina Jones, Audrey Carnes, Aubree Mosby and coaches Lindsey Clark and Taylor Morris. Hancock County will compete in the All 'A' state tournament in Owensboro on April 27.
The Lady Hornets showed what they were made of when they blanked Owensboro Catholic 8-0 in the championship game of the All 'A' Classic 3rd Region Tournament Tuesday at Whitesville. Layni Roberts and Jordyn Waltrip blasted huge home runs and Lily Roberts pitched a complete game shutout.
Hancock County will advance to the All 'A' state tourney to be played at Jack C. Fisher Park in Owensboro on April 27-28.
HCHS coach Dwayne Wroe spoke about his team's performance after the game.
'This is one of the most special wins I've had. We were down a couple of starters and I told them before the game that someone was going to step up, because that's what good teams do. We had some girls do that and I couldn't be more proud of this bunch.'
Roberts struck out the side in the first inning and Catholic's Hannah Robbins was pitching well for the Lady Aces as there was no score through three frames.
Layni Roberts put the Lady Hornets on the scoreboard in the fourth with a monster 2-run shot that cleared the fence in center field. Carolina Jones also scored on the play as she was on as a courtesy runner for Lily Roberts, who led off the inning with a double.
'Layni got us going. When she came up and hit that homer it kind of relaxed us and gave us some breathing room,' Wroe said.
Baylee Estes led off the fifth frame with a triple, but Robbins battled out of trouble and left the speedy junior stranded at third.
The Lady Aces had their chance in the home half of the fifth when Hannah Tignor led off the inning with a double. But Lily Roberts had no intention of allowing a run to score as she set down the next three batters on strikes.
Hancock County wasn't nearly finished offensively and Layni Roberts led off the sixth with a base hit. Emmalynn Higdon smacked a line drive to right field that set up more heroics from the Lady Hornets. Waltrip stepped to the plate and the 8th grader belted a 3-run home run to center field and the route was on.
'Jordyn had been struggling a little bit at the plate and I knew it was just a matter of time before she broke out of it. That was a big time hit for her tonight,' Wroe said.
Catholic went down 1-2-3 in the sixth and Hancock County added three more runs in the top of the seventh. Ella House singled before Layni Roberts ripped an RBI double. Madyson Higdon had a RBI and Aubree Mosby knocked in the final run with a base hit.
Lily then finished off the Lady Aces with a strike out to end the game.
Roberts allowed no runs on two hits, with 17 Ks and two walks over seven innings. Robbins went the distance and absorbed the loss for Catholic.
'We were a little bit worried because of the rain and field conditions and how that was going to be on her (Lily's) knee. But she was a trooper and I can't put into words how valuable she was out there on the mound tonight,' the coach said. 'It was just a great performance by one of the top pitchers in the state. I'm glad she's on our team.'
Layni Roberts was 3 for 3 with a double, home run and three RBI. Waltrip was 2 for 4 with the homer and three RBI, Estes was 1 for 3 with a triple, Lily Roberts (double), Emmalynn Higdon and Mosby were all 1 for 3, and House and Madyson Higdon both went 1 for 4.
Tignor was 2 for 2 for the Lady Aces.
'It's been a while since we've been to All 'A' state and I really wanted these seniors to experience that. It's going to be good for these younger girls, too,' the coach said. 'Hopefully we'll make some noise and bring home a big trophy.'
Three HCHS girls made the All 'A' regional All-Tournament Team and one made Academic all- tourney. They are Jordyn Waltrip, Layni Roberts, Lily Roberts and Kylie Westerfield. A photo of these girls will be published in next week's Clarion.
Trinity The Lady Hornets advanced to the finals of the All 'A' regional with a 5-0 win over Trinity at Whitesville Monday.
Hancock County took a one run lead in the second inning when Layni Roberts scored on an error. The game remained close until Ava Riggs delivered a 2-run triple in the fourth.
HCHS center fielder Kylie Westerfield was injured when a pitch struck her hand while at the plate. The senior suffered a clean break and her availability going forward is unknown.
Audrey Carnes and Emmalynn Higdon gave the girls some extra breathing room with RBI hits in the sixth while pitcher Lily Roberts and the HCHS defense took care of business.
Roberts allowed no runs on four hits with 14 Ks and two walks over seven innings for the win. Sophia Hatfield took the loss for Trinity.
Carnes was 2 for 2 at the plate with one RBI, Riggs was 1 for 3 with the triple and two RBI, Higdon was 1 for 3 with a double and one RBI, Layni Roberts, Lily Roberts and Ella House all went 1 for 3.
Madison McDaniel had three hits for Trinity.
By Steve Wimmer

title: Everbody's Fitness Center gives hope to Parkinson's patients through Exercise
description: This month Everbody's Rock Steady Boxing T
content:
This month Everbody's Rock Steady Boxing Tell City, located at Everbody's Fun & Fitness Center, will join millions in observing Parkinson's Awareness Month. Parkinson's disease is a degenerative movement disorder which can cause deterioration of motor skills, balance, speech and sensory function.
Everbody's RSB Tell City gives those living with Parkinson's disease hope today by offering a non-contact, boxing-inspired fitness routine proving to dramatically improve their quality of life.
According to the Parkinson's Disease Foundation, more than 10 million people worldwide are living with Parkinson's disease and more than 60,000 Americans are diagnosed each year.
'There is strong evidence from clinical research studies that exercise helps Parkinson's disease. Rock Steady Boxing is a proven exercise technique that can be helpful to people with Parkinson's,' said Dr. Steven Gunzler, a neurologist for University Hospitals and assistant professor of neurology at Case Western Reserve University.
Rock Steady Boxing serves participants at all stages of Parkinson's – from the newly diagnosed to those who have been living with the disease for decades. 'We are fortunate to be able to provide this program to the community,' said Laura Schilling, Certified Rock Steady Boxing Coach.
About Everbody's Rock Steady Boxing Tell City Everbody's RSB Tell City officially opened in January, 2022 and currently offers 2 classes a week – Tuesday @10:30AM and Thursday @10:30AM. 'Our classes are designed to accommodate all levels of fitness and disease. We are blessed with dedicated volunteers that help make this possible,' explains Laura, Certified RSB Coach.
Want to learn more about the program? Contact Everbody's Fitness at (812) 547-3565 or email Laura at laura@everbodys.com and help our team 'Fight Back' against Parkinson's disease!

title: Healthy Habits: Calcium & Magnesium Balance
description: The balance of calcium and magnesium, two essential minerals, is very important for optimal health. The two work together to achieve perfect cell metabolism in our bodies. They ar
content:
The balance of calcium and magnesium, two essential minerals, is very important for optimal health. The two work together to achieve perfect cell metabolism in our bodies. They are both positively charged electrolytes and considered 'macro-minerals' because our bodies need more than 100 mg of each daily.
Calcium requires magnesium in order to be properly absorbed. Calcium and magnesium deficiency can cause a resistance to vitamin D absorption.
Perfect Ratio of calcium/magnesium
The recommended calcium/magnesium ratio is 2:1. For example, if you are getting 800 mg of calcium from the foods you eat daily, then you should also be getting around 400 mg of magnesium in your diet as well, for a perfect balance.
Calcium Most are aware that getting enough calcium in our diets is crucial for healthy bones and teeth. Here is a list of some of the other health benefits of calcium: cardioprotective, balances pH (acid/alkaline balance), prevents osteoporosis, helps with maintaining healthy weight, promotes healthy blood pressure, reduces risk of colon cancer & kidney stones and promotes a healthy nervous system.
The recommended daily intake of calcium is around 600-800 mg, and that amount is increased for pregnant women. Here are some of the best whole food sources of calcium: organic whole raw sesame seed butter, lightly steamed dark leafy greens (organic kale & broccoli are great choices), organic sugar-free kefir & yogurt, sardines, organic grass-fed cow's milk & chesses, organic raw almonds and organic okra.
Magnesium Some of you may already know that magnesium is calming and helps with getting a good night's sleep. It can also be a possible remedy for 'restless leg syndrome'. Here are some of magnesium's other benefits: reduces stress, strengthens bones & joints, reduces muscle tension, reduces anxiety, improves cognitive abilities, promotes a healthy immune system, relieves pain & headaches, remedies constipation and helps with digestion of proteins, carbs & fats.
The recommended daily intake of magnesium is around 300-400 mg, and that amount is increased for pregnant women also. Here are some of the best whole food sources of magnesium: organic raw cacao (nibs or powder), organic hemp seeds, organic chia seeds, organic pumpkin seeds and organic wheat germ.
Recipe If you have a tough time eating your dark leafy greens in order to get enough calcium, try making a shake! Here's a great shake recipe for you chocolate lovers that will give you a good amount of calcium and magnesium; Add these ingredients to your blender, blend well and enjoy: A few ice cubes made with filtered water, two cups (or more) of organic unsweetened almond milk or cow's milk, one tablespoon of raw organic cacao powder, one tablespoon of organic raw whole sesame seed butter, one teaspoon of organic finely ground flax seed meal, one half teaspoon of organic spirulina & chlorella powder, one teaspoon of organic kale powder, and some organic local honey to taste.
If the shake is too thick, add filtered water or more milk and blend. Also, you can substitute or add-in: A teaspoon or more of organic wheat germ, a half tablespoon of organic raw whole hemp seed butter, a half tablespoon of organic raw whole pumpkin seed butter, and/or one teaspoon of organic broccoli powder.
Be Well and God Bless You.
By Jennifer Wimmer

title: Getting To Know You: Darrell Wall
description: Darrell Wall was born and raised in Hancock County. He and his wife, Donna, live on a farm in Lewisport that's been in her family since the early 1940s. They live in the heart of District 1, and…
content:
Darrell Wall was born and raised in Hancock County. He and his wife, Donna, live on a farm in Lewisport that's been in her family since the early 1940s.
They live in the heart of District 1, and Darrell Wall is now serving as the new District 1 Lewisport Magistrate to fill the seat vacated by John Garner. He was sworn-in last Friday, and will serve in the position until the election in November and possibly longer if he's elected at that time.
'I care a lot about the district and the people,' Darrell said. 'I will try to make myself readily available to the people. I still do work full-time at Domtar in Hawesville, but Hancock County is in my blood and I want to do the best I can to serve the constituents of that district in whatever is needed.'
He said that a piece of advice he gives out and also tries to live by, is to: Listen intently before you speak. 'I think oftentimes, and even in my past, I was quicker to speak instead of listening,' he said. 'I think listening goes a long way, especially in the position of a magistrate.
You need to be able to listen to people, hear what they're saying and understand their needs. That's how I'll approach this position. I'm going to do my best to uphold their interests.'
Darrell's parents are the late Neal & Ann Wall. 'We actually moved up here in 1969, Dad did, with the construction of Southwire. We moved here as a family and I've been here ever since,' he said. 'I was the type that worked a lot. I played sports up until my freshman year, then I worked on some local farms and I worked with my dad in several different small businesses.'
He graduated in the Class of 1982 from Hancock County High School. He attended Rets Electronic Institute in Louisville earning his Associate's Degree in Electronics in 1987. He's been working in industrial maintenance since graduating. In addition to working at Domtar, he has also worked at Commonwealth (Martin Marietta at that time) and the Big Rivers Coleman Station.
He is currently an Electrician at Domtar and has gained extensive knowledge over the years of the inner workings of industry. He has served as the President of the local United Steel Workers Union in Hawesville (Local USW # 1261) for the past 6 years. His term is ending in the next week, which he said will free him up more to be dedicated in his service as District 1 Magistrate.
Darrell & Donna are blessed with 3 children and one grandchild. 'Our oldest is Taylor. He lives in Denver, Colorado. Our middle child, Rebecca, is married to Zayne Boling. Our grandson, Leyton, was born on February 26th, 2024.
Our youngest daughter, Anna, still lives at home and is in college. She is finishing this year working at North Hancock Elementary and attending OCTC. She will transfer to Western KY University-Owensboro Campus in the fall,' he said.
When their son, Taylor, attended Hancock County High School, he played basketball and football and they were very instrumental in helping with fundraisers and supporting the HC Hornets.
Rebecca & Zayne live only about a mile away from them and they are savoring the blessing of being grandparents right now. They enjoy spending time on their farm and spending time with family and friends.
They purchased Donna's family home when they purchased her family's farm and have turned that into an Airbnb (Bed & Breakfast). Donna's parents are the late O.T. & Shirley Young. They lease the farmland, but there is still a lot of mowing and upkeep, and they both stay very busy.
By Jennifer Wimmer

title: Fiscal Court Outlines Plans for Roadways; County set to receive $10,242,000
description: On Thursday, April 17th, Representativ
content:
On Thursday, April 17th, Representative Scott Lewis announced more than $10M in state funding returning to Hancock County to invest in roadways and essential infrastructure, as reported in last week's edition of The Clarion.
Judge-Executive Johnny Roberts outlined what projects the Hancock County Fiscal Court has planned for these dollars saying, 'The current Hwy 60 widening is in the plan now and we're hoping that finishes in the fall of this year.'
Widening from KY-1957 into Lewisport
Widening from KY-1957 into Lewisport Roberts continued, 'We talked about adding to the new plan what we'd like to see and some of our priorities are, number one: to continue that widening from 1957 on into Lewisport. We have a couple of places in that area that are dangerous with truck traffic.'
Bridge Approach
Bridge Approach The other project the court is prioritizing is the bridge approach. 'Several years ago,' Roberts said, 'the state had bought property and easements and right of ways, and we're trying to get them to finish that.
There has been money put into both of those projects. This is a multi-year plan (FY2024 and FY2025), so there will have to be money added to those projects to finish, probably.'
Resurfacing of Hwy 60 Eastbound Lane
Resurfacing of Hwy 60 Eastbound Lane 'Those were 2 of the main projects we talked about,' he said, 'and also the resurfacing of Hwy 60 on the eastbound lane that they're currently not working on that had some bad spots. And we had some small projects with some guardrails in it, and also we had $171K of discretionary funds approved for Crowe Road. That road is not in great shape so that will be a big improvement for that as well.'
State Road Plan
State Road Plan The state road plan provides: $2.1M in FY25 to improve the connection between US-60 and the Cannelton Bridge approach at Hawesville, $24K in FY25 to install guardrails on KY-261, $525K in FY24 and $5.25M in FY25 toward pavement conditions on US-60, and $900K in FY25 and $1.25M in FY26 to widen US-60 from Lewisport to KY-1957.
Local Road Projects – Old Mill Rd. & Crowe Rd.
Local Road Projects – Old Mill Rd. & Crowe Rd. House Joint Resolution 92 includes $193,000 for Hancock County – $22K in FY25 to resurface Old Mill Rd., and $171K in FY25 to resurface Crowe Rd.
For further information on the 2024 Regular Session or to learn more about the Kentucky General Assembly, visit legislature.ky.gov.
By Jennifer Wimmer

title: Roberts goes deep as Lady Hornets win 11-0
description: Kylie Westerfield shows the signed cast on her broken hand while leading the chants in the Lady Hornets' dugout. The Lady Hornets bounced back after two loses with an impressive, 11-0 win in five…
content:
Kylie Westerfield shows the signed cast on her broken hand while leading the chants in the Lady Hornets' dugout.
The Lady Hornets bounced back after two loses with an impressive, 11-0 win in five innings over Butler County at Morgantown Tuesday. Lily Roberts hit a home run and was the winning pitcher. Roberts got the offense going when she smacked a homer to right field in the second inning.
Emmalynn Higdon later ripped a double to score Ava Riggs and Jordyn Waltrip. Higdon scored on a grounder by Baylee Estes and the score was 4-0.
Estes delivered a 2-run triple in the fourth and Bella Bryant followed with an RBI base hit. Layni Roberts and Riggs knocked in a run each and Waltrip hit a sacrifice fly for an RBI.
Lily Roberts added one more run on a hit to center field and the defense finished off the home team in the fifth inning.
Roberts allowed no runs on three hits, with nine Ks and no walks through five frames.
Lily was 3 for 3 at the plate with the home run and three RBI. Higdon was 2 for 3 with a double and two RBI, Bryant was 1 for 1 with one RBI, Aubree Mosby was 1 for 1, Waltrip was 1 for 2 with one RBI, Layni Roberts was 1 for 3, Estes was 1 for 4 with the triple and three RBI, and Ella House was 1 for 4.
Carolina Jones and Madyson Higdon both scored one run each.
Muhlenberg County The Lady Hornets had their 5-game winning streak snapped when they lost 1-0 to Muhlenberg County in extra innings Friday at Vastwood Park.
The game was a pitcher's duel between two of the top throwers in the area in Hancock County's Lily Roberts and the Lady Mustangs' Ava Carver.
'It was a tough loss, but we don't have anyone to blame but ourselves,' HCHS coach Dwayne Wroe said. 'Lily pitched another great game. We just have to give her some run support.'
Muhlenberg had a base runner in scoring position in the first inning, but Roberts ended the frame with a strike out. The senior from Lewisport struck out the side in the second and third innings. Baylee Estes had a bunt single and stole second base in the third, but was left stranded.
The Lady Hornets offense did not produce a run, but they easily could have if not for several impressive defensive plays made by the visitors.
Ella House hit a line drive that was caught by the right fielder and Emmalynn Higdon lined out to the Mustangs' second baseman. Higdon and Audrey Carnes also made good catches of their own while in the field.
Madyson Higdon and Estes led off the sixth inning with line drives that were caught. Muhlenberg short stop Joshlynn Noe made a spectacular diving catch to rob Estes.
Carnes and House followed with 2-out hits, but the girls were eventually left on base. Layni Roberts led off the seventh with a hit and Ava Riggs sacrificed Roberts to second base, but the next two batters struck out.
By rule, the Lady Mustangs started the extra inning with a runner at second base. She advanced to third on a wild pitch then scored on a ground ball hit to second.
Emmalynn Higdon started the home half of the 8th at second base. Her sister Madyson moved her to third on a sacrifice bunt, but the next two Hancock batters struck out to end the game.
Carver got the win, allowing no runs on four hits, with eight Ks and no walks over eight innings. Roberts took the loss, allowing one run on three hits, with 12 Ks and three walks.
'She (Carver) is good and she kept us off balance with off-speed stuff,' Wroe said.
Layni Roberts and House were both 1 for 3 at the plate. Estes and Carnes both went 1 for 4.
'We had some people up in good situations and we didn't come through. We had too many called third strikes. You have to be aggressive with two strikes and put the ball in play. You have to want it,' the coach said.
The Lady Hornets will compete in the All 'A' state tournament in Owensboro this weekend.
McLean County The Lady Hornets scored eight runs in the first inning and went on to win by a final score of 19-4 over McLean County at Calhoun last Thursday.
Baylee Estes led off the game with a hit and things went downhill for the Lady Cougars after that.
Lily Roberts delivered a 2-run double, Jordyn Waltrip had an RBI hit and Aubree Mosby knocked in two runs with a line drive. Estes scored Emmalynn Higdon on a ground ball, Mosby scored on a wild pitch and Audrey Carnes capped off the inning with an RBI single to left field.
McLean's highlight of the game was Abigail Walker's home run to center field off Roberts. Lily hit the next batter then the senior hurler struck out the next two batters to end the frame.
Hancock County plated six more runs in the second inning on hits by Waltrip, Mosby, Estes, and Ella House.
The Lady Hornets strung together four consecutive hits in the third inning and a few walks later the score was 19-1.
Roberts gave way to 8th grader Ryleigh French and the youngster gave up a few hits before finishing the game with a strike out!
Lily got the win while allowing one run on one hit, with four Ks and no walks in two innings. French allowed three runs (one earned) on five hits, with one K and no walks. Macie Geel took the loss for MCHS.
Estes was 3 for 4 at the plate with four runs scored, and Mosby was 2 for 2 with four RBI. Waltrip was 2 for 2 with two RBI, Bella Bryant was 1 for 1 with two RBI, Carnes was 1 for 2 with two RBI, Ansley House was 1 for 1 with one RBI, Ella House and Lily Roberts (double) both with 1 for 3 with two RBI each, Higdon was 1 for 1 with three runs scored, Layni Roberts scored three runs, Carolina Jones scored two runs, Riggs scored a run and French had one RBI.
Meade County Meade County out hit Hancock County 10 to 3 during a 6-1 win for the Lady Wave over the Lady Hornets at Vastwood Monday.
Meade scored a run in the first inning then added more in the third through sixth frames. Hancock's lone run came in the fourth on an RBI double by Bella Bryant. Ella House singled and scored from first base on the play.
Lily Roberts absorbed the loss. She allowed four runs (three earned) on six hits, with three Ks and three walks in 3.1 innings on the mound. Bryant allowed two runs (none earned) on four hits, with one K and no walks in 3.2 innings of relief. Veronica Roberts was the winner. She allowed one run on three hits, with 13 Ks and no walks over seven frames. Bryant was 1 for 2 with the double and one RBI. House and Baylee Estes both went 1 for 3.
Autumn Rodgers was 4 for 4 for Meade County.
By Steve Wimmer

title: Brent Wigginton selected as District 1 Magistrate Candidate
description: The Hancock County Republican Party has selected Brent Wigginton as their candidate to run against the Democrat candidate, Darrell Wall, in November for Lewisport (District 1) Magistrate. Brent served…
content:
The Hancock County Republican Party has selected Brent Wigginton as their candidate to run against the Democrat candidate, Darrell Wall, in November for Lewisport (District 1) Magistrate.
Brent served the City of Lewisport for 22 years. He was hired by the City in 2001 for the Public Works position as operator of gas, water and sewer, and for 16 years served as Lewisport City Administrator. He was also a volunteer firefighter at the Lewisport Volunteer Fire Department for many years.
He retired in 2022, but is still very active in the City. He continues to serve on the Heritage Festival and Christmas in the Park Committees, and is also a member of the Lewisport Lions Club. Since 2010, he has been a Kenergy Board Representative for Hancock County, and is the current General Manager of Daviess County Water District.
In his many years of public service, Brent has served both the citizens of Lewisport and of Hancock County. 'I always felt like being a magistrate is something I wanted to do,' he said, 'it's been a goal of mine for many years.'
Having served in city government, it has given him many years of experience in dealing with challenges such as with finding funding for projects, audits, budgets, etc. 'It is just instilled in me,' he said, 'it's almost like second nature anymore, and that would just transfer over into doing the same with the county. I'm very well prepared to be able to do a good job not only for District 1, but for the County as a whole.'
Brent grew up farming with his parents, Jerry & Kay Wigginton, in Pellville and graduated from Hancock County High School in 1988. He attended Owensboro Vocational School and studied machine and shop while at HCHS. After graduation, he was a Production Machinist at the G.E. plant in Owensboro while also part-time farming for 8 years, until beginning his job with the City of Lewisport.
He and his wife, Renee Shutt Wigginton, were high school sweethearts and married in 1990. She has been an RN at Owensboro Health Regional Hospital for almost 40 years. Their daughter Raelynn and her husband, Russell Haycraft, live nearby. Raelynn teaches 7th Grade English at HCMS, and they have blessed Brent & Renee with a granddaughter, Collins Rae Haycraft, and a newborn grandson, Micah Walker Haycraft.
Their youngest daughter, Haley Ann Wigginton, is graduating in December with a Bachelor's Degree in Hospitality Management at Western Kentucky University, and is Assistant Manager at Olde Stone Country Club in Bowling Green.
Brent was involved for many years with the Hancock County Softball Rec. League, and for 14 years with the HC Softball Boosters while his daughters were growing up. 'We had to work hand in hand with the Parks System,' he said. 'I'm well in tune with the Parks Dept. and the importance of our parks and how much they're used by the public, as well as their partnership with the school system.'
HC Democrat Party Candidate
The Hancock County Democrat Party selected Darrell Wall as their candidate to fill former District 1 Magistrate John Garner's seat after he resigned to serve as School Resource Officer at North Hancock Elementary. Wall was then sworn-in as the new Lewisport (District 1) Magistrate, and will serve until the election on November 5th.
Wall will hold office, as the Governor appointed candidate, until a candidate is elected at the General Election on November 5th, 2024. The newly elected individual in November will take office immediately and fill the unexpired term.
Independent Independent Candidates may pick up the nomination forms at the Hancock County Clerk's Office. The nomination form must be submitted by the June 4th, 2024 filing deadline to be voted on in November.
Write-Ins Any qualified individual may run as a write-in candidate as long as they file a declaration on intent in the Clerk's office by October 25th. Their name will not appear on the ballot. It will be up to the voter to write the candidate's name on the ballot next to the coordinating office. Only votes for candidates who have filed the proper write-in filing paper will be counted.
By Jennifer Wimmer

title: A family business for 78 years- Fischer's is the Go-To Store
description: Fischer's Furniture and Appliance, a family business for 78 years now, is still going strong. Owners, Richard Fischer, Betty (Fischer), J.T. Hagedorn and Jared Hagedorn (3rd generation) continue their…
content:
Fischer's Furniture and Appliance, a family business for 78 years now, is still going strong. Owners, Richard Fischer, Betty (Fischer), J.T. Hagedorn and Jared Hagedorn (3rd generation) continue their family's proud legacy of service to the local communities in Perry, Spencer, Hancock, Breckinridge, Ohio counties and more.
The company boasts a 40,000 square foot showroom (one of the largest in the area) showcasing quality furniture, appliances, outdoor power equipment, bedding, home décor, grilling and more.
The also have a fully stocked small engine parts and plumbing supply department, called Plumber's Alley, located in the 'alley' behind the store, but still accessible from inside the store as well. This department supplies contractors, plumbers, mechanics and 'do it yourselfers' with the parts to get their job done from one convenient location.
Appliances and Furniture Fischer's provides it's customers with
best in industry appliances such as; Frigidaire Gallery, Frigidaire Professional, Electrolux, Kitchen Aid, Maytag, Whirlpool, Samsung, Speed Queen, General Electric, Amana and Midea.
Their quality lineup of furniture gives customers the 'look' they want; custom upholstery from Flexsteel, Home Stretch and Best Chair. Lane, Riverside, Liberty, Intercon, New Classic, Style Craft and other lines, completes Fischer's lineup of furniture brands.Global flooring providers
Fischer's also provides floor products from global flooring providers, Mohawk and Shaw Floors, two of the largest in the country.
Fischer's Outdoor Equipment Now for tending to the outside of your home, Fischer's has been a dealer for Echo Power Equipment, SCAG and Toro lawn equipment for years. They have mechanics on hand year-round to handle 'Service after the Sale.'
Grilling Equipment
Fischer's also carries a full line of Big Green Egg products and Broil King with PGT (Performance Grilling Technology), gas and pellet grills. They are you're one stop shop for all your grilling needs!
Builders, property owners, remodelers and interior designers 'We not only work with homeowners, we work with builders, property managers, remodelers and interior designers as well,' says Betty Fischer. Fischer's delivers and installs appliances, furniture, and floor covering with experienced personnel. We have a service tech to take care of the appliances purchased.'
Fischer's 'Service after the Sale' motto is one Fischer's takes seriously.
'Service after the Sale' motto is one Fischer's takes seriously. 'We care about our customers. We listen to their needs and work with them to satisfy that need during the purchase and after the sale,' said Jarad Hagedorn.
Fischer's has a friendly, very caring staff and fantastic selection of home products which makes the store a one-stop-shop or better yet, your 'Go To Store'. The Showroom is located at located at 910 Main Street, Tell City, Indiana.
Visit gofischers.com for product info and special promotions.
