title: Healthy Habits: Loss
description: Yorktown, Virginia is where that final battle in the American Revolutionary War happened and our first President of the United States, George Washington, led the Continental Army to victory. Please…
content:
Yorktown, Virginia is where that final battle in the American Revolutionary War happened and our first President of the United States, George Washington, led the Continental Army to victory. Please take out last week's printed edition of The Clarion (7-4-2024) and, on page 1, mark out 'New York' and write 'Virginia'.
My dad, the late Donn Wimmer, would've laughed about the typo I made last week. He was always so gracious about errors. I appreciated him so much for many reasons, and one was that he was very understanding about mistakes. Dad was a patriot and taught me to love my country too. This was a hard holiday to experience without him. Nevertheless, it is healthy to be patriotic. Why wouldn't we be proud of our country? It is healthy to love your nation, wherever you live. Patriotism is healthy, not to be confused with nationalism.
At first, it seemed almost impossible to type articles or do any of this without Dad here. Loss causes grief and that is something that has some layers to it. I'm discovering as I move forward with this work, that I can actually feel close to Dad through the writing.
There has been so much loss. We could never truly thank enough all those who have sacrificed their lives to gain our independence, or the countless who have given their lives since then to make sure we've kept it.
Since 2020, most of us have lost at least one loved one. We have experienced an incredible amount of loss. How do we cope with it? How do we carry on in their absence? It is never easy to lose the people we love, and we can never truly prepare for it. Once they are gone, we must face living without them. The full realization of that loss causes us to grieve.
The grieving process can make us feel like we are being torn apart. It can feel like a part of us is missing, that life can never be happy again, or even cause us to feel angry. The Swiss-American psychiatrist Elizabeth Kubler-Ross, in her best-selling book 'On Death and Dying', presented 5 stages of grief: denial, anger, bargaining, depression and, finally, acceptance.
Everyone copes with grief differently; everyone is unique. Extroverts may find it more comforting to be surrounded by people. Introverts, however, may find it very hard to grieve with people around at all. What is comforting to one, could be counterproductive for another. However long it takes you to grieve is o.k., but don't stay there. Switch over to knowing that your 'loss' is actually their gain, because they are now celebrating in Heaven. Be joyful for them.
Nothing compares to the great love God has for us, and nothing compares to the healing balm that He is always extending to us. We can lean into Him and realize that His love has not gone away, even though some of our loved ones have. And, we can also realize that our loved ones who are no longer here are now being completely enveloped in His unconditional love.
We can find some relief in knowing that. We can decide to be joyful for those who are no longer with us in this world of toil and snare, as it is referred to in the old gospel hymn 'Just a Closer Walk with Thee'. . .'Who with me, my burden shares? None but thee. Oh Dear Lord, none but thee.'
We can take some comfort in knowing that our loved ones who have passed from this world are no longer struggling. Mother's Day and Father's Day were celebrated recently, but for some it was a day of missing parents who've passed away. We miss them dearly and we weren't ready to say goodbye, but we are happy to know they are in a better place.
They are no longer in pain. They are in Heaven with long lost loved ones and, most importantly, with God. He is wrapping His Mighty arms around them now and showering them with a love so great that there truly aren't words adequate to describe it. He sent His Son to die for us so that whosoever believes will be saved. We have that guarantee.
We must always put God first in our lives. If we allow His Great Love to move through us, we can spread that love and light into this dark world and onto our loved ones who are STILL HERE. We are called to be One Body of Christ Jesus, united and working together, while our departed loved ones are singing God's praises in Heaven with His angels, and are awaiting our arrival to that Promised Home.
Matthew 6:33 tells us, 'But seek ye first the Kingdom of God, and His Righteousness, and All these things shall be added unto you.'. . .It is the relationship with God and putting Him first in our lives that is essential. Our loved ones who are no longer with us, they know this and want us to be focused on God, not them. They know that His Joy is our strength, and we need His strength to keep marching on. They want us to be joyful, not sorrowful.
Take comfort in the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. No matter what you're going through in life, whether you are grieving the loss of a loved one, or struggling in some other way, God will get you through it. He loves you. Give Him your heart today. He will never leave you or forsake you. Christ Jesus will walk with you, talk with you and never leave your side as you continue your journey through this world.
It is only such a short time, really, that we are actually here, and an eternity in Heaven to look forward to. Get busy living for God and doing His will, and the time will pass quicker. Keep marching onward. Don't be bogged down with grief. It's our common enemy who wants us down and out, with our heads down, and that doesn't bring our departed loved ones joy, and it doesn't give Glory to God.
Start praising God and thanking Him for delivering them from this time of tribulation, and continue to stand strong in Christ Jesus. Taking that stance will honor them. We are more than conquerors (Romans 8:37). We are overcomers through Christ Jesus. We can do ALL things through Him, who strengthens us.
~Be Well and God Bless You.
By Jennfier Wimmer

title: An Essay By HCHS Graduate James Singleton
description: Along the Ohio River, Hancock County, Kentucky, has created a strong industrial and economic liveliness throughout its history. Hancock...
content:
Along the Ohio River, Hancock County, Kentucky, has created a strong industrial and economic liveliness throughout its history. Hancock County is small but rich in heritage, land, and hospitality, as stated by the Hancock County Industrial Foundation. Hancock County is conveniently located between Owensboro and Louisville along with the Bob Cummins Lincoln Trail Bridge in Hawesville creating easy and simple travel to Indiana and I-64. Hancock County's history began on January 3, 1829, when Kentucky Governor Thomas Metcalfe signed into law a statute forming Hancock County from parts of Breckinridge, Daviess, and Ohio counties, making it the 85th county of Kentucky. Hancock was named after John Hancock, the most notable patriot who signed the Declaration of Independence.
The Industrial Foundation goes to explain that Hancock's County seat of Hawesville was donated by Richard Hawes in 1830 along with the first post office. As the county grew, Lewisport was founded in 1839 on the edge of U.S. Highway 60 about 18 miles away from Owensboro. The town was originally called 'Little Yellow Banks' but later changed to its current name in honor of John Lewis.
According to the Industrial Foundation from the start, the Ohio River has been the center of industry in Hancock County. Steamboat construction was the first industry to enter the county along with a thriving coal mining industry made the town one of the biggest refueling centers on the river. Hancock County made John Cannon's name notable as one of the first riverboat builders and captain. Cannon's fastest boat, the Robert E. Lee, won the most famous steamboat race ever held in America on July 4th, 1870. As the steamboat industry grew Captain W.D. Crammond operated the H&C (Hawesville and Cannelton) ferry and built four steamboats in Hawesville and ran a packet service on the river. Another notable steamboat engineer was Arthur Rees of Hawesville, an engineer on many Ohio River steamboats, including the Belle of Louisville. As the population of Hancock County grew, industry flourished especially on the river. Residents in Hancock County crossed the river on the Hawesville ferry, which was opened in 1831. Residents in Hancock County crossed the river on the Hawesville ferry, which was opened in 1831. In 1892 J.W. Pate began one of the largest ferry operations for its era after John Crammond leased the ferry rights. Earl Bettinger then assumed operation in the 1930s. As ferry operations grew the H&C became the largest ferry operation in Kentucky before it shut down in 1966 when the Lincoln Trail Bridge opened.
The Ohio River has been an important factor in the growth and development of Hancock County. The river created the most important means of transportation and connection to the outside world before the railroads were created. (Hancock County Industrial Foundation) The river was the gateway to foundational industries such as steamboat manufacturing and coal mining which led to more industries coming into the county to create the staple of economic and industrial flourishment that Hancock County is today. Hancock County is now one of the most economic counties in Kentucky and would not be where it is today without the advancements and sacrifices of its early settlers.
By James Singleton

title: Nancy's Notes: The Bullies
description: We are now watching the attempted assassination of Donald Trump. In interviews those who knew the shooter, some who went to school with him said he was terribly bullied. What makes a bully? Most often…
content:
We are now watching the attempted assassination of Donald Trump. In interviews those who knew the shooter, some who went to school with him said he was terribly bullied. What makes a bully? Most often he has a low opinion of himself, probably by being bullied at some point in his life. In order to rise himself up, he has to put someone down.
Some victims feel so worthless they are actually committing suicide. It happened to a relative of mine. He was only 14-years-old. The family only found out about the bullying at the funeral, where fellow students told how bad the bullying had been. If only someone had told someone.
If someone had reported the bully who shot at Trump would it have changed the outcome of the shooting? Would it have saved the innocent bystander who died protecting his family?
Some school shootings have been executed by students who were bullied, some as young as 14. Some parents are now incarcerated for making the gun available. And who needs an assault rifle in a house where there are children?
Some kids have no concept of death. When I went to visit my 8-year-old grandson, he was playing a video game where he was shooting and killing human like characters. 'Why would you want to shoot and kill people?' I asked. 'Oh, it's okay Nanny. They'll be alive tomorrow,' he said. I had to explain once a person is dead he will never be alive again.
Now he is a very good husband and father. He would never allow his kids to play sniper video games at a young age. Some of the school shooters killed themselves. It was reported they were avid video game players. Did they think it was okay and that they would be alive tomorrow?
The shooter was a very good shot. Where did he learn to shoot that well? If Trump had not turned his head at that crucial moment, he would not be here today.
For awhile I had a foster child. He had been socially suppressed. Just about every day I would hear tires screeching on the street in front of our house and I knew James had run out in front of a car. No amount of telling him the dangers would help. One night a coon ran in front of my car and I ran over it. I got James out of the car and showed him what could happen if he ran in front of a car. I kicked it around and showed him what dead was all about. He never ran in front of a car again.
Sometimes we take it for granted that kids know, but sometimes they don't. They see a movie where someone gets killed and the next day another movie shows them alive. What are their young minds going to think?
Bullies can be classmates, siblings, other relatives, neighbors or even parents. They need to be discovered. Encourage your child to let you know if it happens to them. Both the bully and the victim need counseling. If someone had told a teacher or parent, my cousin Kaleb and his bullies could have gotten help and that sweet, loving Kaleb would still be here today.
By Nancy Marlow Moffett

title: Labor Day Weekend Fest planned for City of Lewisport
description: The Lewisport City Council met on Thursday evening, July 18th. At last month's meeting, it was approved for there to be a Labor Day...
content:
The Lewisport City Council met on Thursday evening, July 18th. At last month's meeting, it was approved for there to be a Labor Day Weekend Fest in downtown Lewisport on Saturday, August 31st. There will be fireworks, a tractor pull and a car show, since those were rained out for the 2024 Annual Lewisport Heritage Festival held in June.
The City plans to have this fun family event from 5:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m., and there will also be food, music and a beer wagon. More information will be provided soon in The Clarion as more details are solidified by the organizing committee and approved by the Council.
New Rides Company
The Heritage Festival Committee has chosen a new rides company for next year's festival, Lewisport Mayor Chad Gregory said. More details on that will also be provided in future editions of The Clarion.
Discussion on Alley Closing (Flener & Adams)
The Council had some discussion on a request that was made by landowners in the City of Lewisport. 'It's a couple of landowners that want the alleys closed,' Gregory said. 'One was not developed and one is developed. The Council decided to table the discussion until, hopefully, we can hear from both of the landowners on why they want this done, and what purpose it will serve.'
Public Works Update
Superintendent R.J. Simpson reported that their summer help has been doing very well and he, the crew, and the Council are very proud of them. He vocalized to the Council last month the need to expand the Public Works building by 30 feet due to the crew's growing amount of equipment. Estimates for construction have not yet been presented. The Council is currently looking at purchasing more pieces of equipment that are needed for the crew, including a dump truck.
By Jennifer Wimmer

title: Healthy Habits: Heat & Cold Therapy
description: You're probably familiar with the acronym RICE, which stands for: Rest,
content:
You're probably familiar with the acronym RICE, which stands for: Rest, Ice, Compression (gentle compressions to bring fresh blood flow and oxygen to the area), and Elevation (propping up the affected area/raising above the heart).
RICE is handy for remembering what to do for acute pain, specifically. For new injuries with temporary/acute pain, ice can alleviate some of that pain as well as helping to keep down the swelling in the first 48 to 72 hours. Heat, however, can be a better choice for chronic pain, which is not caused by an immediate injury, and is ongoing. Heat and cold can both help alleviate pain, depending on the individual situation, and there are times when switching back and forth can be beneficial as well (contrast therapy).
Cold Therapy
Cold therapy, also known as cryotherapy, soothes injured muscles, joints, and tissues. It decreases pain, promotes healing, can help prevent further injury, and reduces swelling and inflammation. Cold compression treatment can also help muscles repair themselves, and it reduces muscle spasms.
Ice packs, ice massage and, yes, the ice bath/ice water plunge are some of the options with cold therapy. If you're brave enough, and your doc has given you the go ahead, you could try out the cold-plunging therapy right in your own home, as long as you have a tub, running water and a freezer to make some ice cubes. There's really no need to travel to the arctic, unless you just want to. With the heat the way it is right now though, it actually might be a great time for travelling north!
Cold-plunging boosts the immune system, supports lymphatic drainage, promotes healthy metabolism, boosts brain health/cognitive function, and stimulates a healthy inflammatory response. Ice baths also stimulate the parasympathetic nervous system, promote a good night's sleep, elevate mood, enhance impulse control, and improve circulation.
There are some listed dos and don'ts for ice bathing. The temperature should not be so cold that it causes pain, of course, and don't stay in for too long. Also, don't ice water plunge right before you want to go to sleep, and don't warm up too quickly afterward; Allow your body some time to warm back up gradually. Some other possible benefits of cold plunging are: boosts energy, increases resilience, reduces chronic pain, and helps regulate the nervous system.
If you're a coward like me when it comes to cold, you can still gain some of these health benefits by, for instance, turning the shower to cold and just holding your head under the cold water for a couple of minutes or less. If you can manage to stand in a cold shower for a couple of minutes at the end before getting out, you'll experience many of the same health benefits of an ice bath. It's a great way to 'wake up' your brain in the morning as well, and promotes healthy hair and skin.
Heat Therapy
Saunas, hot tubs, heating pads, hot compresses, hot stone massage therapy, hot showers, and hot baths promote relaxation and relieve soreness. Heat therapy can also improve your mental state, promote better sleep, accelerate healing, decrease joint pain, increase metabolism, improve circulation, and promote the flow of endorphins. Make sure the temperature is not too hot; Don't overdo it.
Contrast Therapy
Contrast therapy, as mentioned above, is alternating between hot and cold therapy. Both hot and cold therapy stimulate your body's natural healing response. You can apply a hot pack or heating pad, then apply the cold pack, and then back to the hot pack, and so on. You can also take a hot bath or shower, and then gradually cool the water until it is as cold as you are comfortable with.
Contraindications
There are some precautions to consider with hot and/or cold therapies, such as if you have any open wounds, infections, sensitive areas, or areas with poor blood circulation. Do your research and talk with your doc first before trying something new if you're not sure.
~Be Well and God Bless You.
By Jennifer Wimmer

title: A Mother and Son's Triumph and Defeat in Maintaining Health
description: Charlotte Martin (72), of Daviess County, has had an incredibly challenging experience over the last couple of decades with managin
content:
Charlotte Martin (72), of Daviess County, has had an incredibly challenging experience over the last couple of decades with managing her own health and her son's. She is a cancer survivor, and since winning that battle has learned to change her diet to lose weight and become much healthier.
After her son, Brian Bivins II (20), was severely injured from a round of childhood immunizations, she discovered that much of what is widely accepted about medicine and diet in the Unites States should be examined more thoroughly.
'It's been several months ago that I actually gave up everything unhealthy – no sugar, no carbs, no grain because they hybridized our grain making it very harmful,' she said. 'I went from a size 18 to a size 10, and it was just from giving up the sugar, carbs and grains. I feel so much better now, and have so much more energy.'
Charlotte had been struggling with her weight, and knew she had to do something. She became a mom again at age 52, when she was asked to babysit for Brian when he was only 5-days-old. They never returned to pick him up, and she's been his mother ever since. He'll be 21 this month.
'A few years ago, I went to the BBQ Festival with my granddaughter,' she said. 'We couldn't find a place to actually sit on a chair so I sat down on the ground on the curb to eat my sandwich and it took 3 men to pull me back up.'
Now that she's been eating healthier, and has been able to shed the extra weight she said, 'Last week, I dropped my telephone going through my son's room and it plopped under the bed. I had to get down to get it, and I got right back up. I couldn't believe it. My son couldn't believe it. We were looking like, 'Oh no, what have I done. I'm on the floor.' And, I got right back up.'
Brian, on the other hand, is still struggling every day with the side effects of the immunizations he was given as a child. After many tests, he was eventually diagnosed with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS).
'He got horribly injured from his childhood immunizations,' Charlotte said. 'They have to take them to go to school. It was time for him to start school, and I took him to our doctor here. He said, 'Charlotte, he is disgustingly healthy.' I said, 'I know. He can run like Forrest Gump, and people marvel at him with his God given athletic abilities.' He would put eighth graders to shame playing basketball, baseball, football, you name it.'
She said the doctor walked out, and the nurse came in with a tray of needles.
'I didn't know anything; I just trusted the doctor,' she said. 'I didn't count how many needles. I didn't ask what was in it; I didn't ask anything. We laughed through it because I kept him laughing through the entire ordeal, and that was the last hour of his life that he was healthy. He never got to play again. He never got to go to school again. We did not know what hit us.'
Brian was bedridden after that day, and still is mostly bedridden to this day.
'All I could do was take care of him,' she said. 'I had to homeschool him.'
This experience opened Charlotte's eyes to other areas, such as with our daily diets. She had gotten very unhealthy and overweight eating the 'American diet' over the years and had finally had enough. She began researching and discovered the dangers of many foods that were toxic but eaten daily by many Americans. She has applied her knowledge in helping her son eat healthier but he continues to suffer terribly, she said.
She said she has no doubt that the immunizations Brian received that day many years ago are responsible for his long-term illness. And, no one has ever been held accountable, and no compensation has been made.
'The highest ranking officer in the military, Admiral Mike Mullen, hunted me down because he wanted me to come to Fort Campbell and speak about it,' she said. 'God did that. And, Tonya Grace wrote about it in Kentucky New Era. I pray every day for God to just let me listen to Him so closely that I will go when He wants me to go, where He wants me to go, say what He wants me to say, and do what He wants me to do.'
Millions worldwide have had similar tragic experiences over the decades, and she considers it her mission in life to raise awareness, and encourages parents and caregivers to do their research, rather than just assuming that the doctors are always correct. For example, ask for the ingredient list for each immunization, and research to find out how many are documented as having suffered injuries from each specific one.
Charlotte and Brian live in Daviess County. She is his full-time caregiver. She has worked many jobs over the years, including as a Legal Assistant to one of the leading medical malpractice lawyers in the country, Daryl Keith, at Wagner and Keith Medical Malpractice Firm in Fort Worth, Texas. She also volunteered as a Writer for a number of years at the Vanderburgh Independent Press – VIP News.
By Jennifer Wimmer

title: Healthy Habits: Wholesome Entertainment
description: August is another hot month, and sometimes that requires doing indoor activities with the family. School doesn't start back up until the 26th for students at HC S
content:
August is another hot month, and sometimes that requires doing indoor activities with the family. School doesn't start back up until the 26th for students at HC Schools, and there are very few wholesome tv shows and movies offered for children and families, in my opinion.
I was very thankful to find Angel Studios in the last year. I have discovered wonderful content on their app, and I want to tell you a little about it, in case you didn't already know. What we watch and listen to does impact our wellness, and taking the time to choose positive content to watch and listen to is definitely a healthy habit to establish.
You may be familiar with The Chosen series. All four seasons were filmed by Angel Studios. Did you know Angel.com is an app you can get and watch episodes of The Chosen for free?
The app offers free episodes of many of the Studios' movies and shows, including some great children's content such as the animation Young David. Contributors 'pay it forward' for episodes of The Chosen and other shows like Young David to be watched on the app for free.
One of the most awesome things we found when we first downloaded the app, were tons of video testimonials titled 'Stories' that adults and children have sent in for the public to watch/listen to. Our favorites were the Stories submitted from viewers about watching The Chosen series. Viewers were saying that it either brought them to God for the first time, or that it renewed their faith.
I realize The Chosen is a theatrical production and that many scenes have been added that are not in Bible Scripture. Honestly, the last season (season 4) really made me angry. There were scenes that I was furious with the director for adding. However, they do make it very clear that it is not solely based on Scripture. There are study guides available that reference exactly what Scriptures each scene is based on, with those listed for the viewer to read. The series was not created with an intention to replace reading the Bible, rather it should be an encouragement for viewers to go and read the Bible for themselves.
Angel Guild
I recently became an Angel Guild Member with Angel Studios, and I highly recommend it. There is an option for a monthly or a yearly membership. The membership includes a discount on books and other items that go along with the children's shows, such as workbooks, stickers, t-shirts, and plushies (stuffed animals), as well as merchandise that complements The Chosen series, and more.
The membership also offers opportunities to vote, such as on which pilot episodes are aired, and which movies will hit the big screen. This adds another way for parents to spend time with their children in reviewing and voting together. We've had a lot of fun with this feature. There are free movie tickets to claim for upcoming showings that you can use or give away, and many other membership perks.
One of the shows that we voted on together is a spectacular wildlife and nature show with outstanding cinematography and phenomenally detailed narrating, with tons of educational content that we are super excited about, called The Riot and the Dance.
They also have 'Dry Bar Comedy' that adults and older children can enjoy together, and there are options available to vote on those hilarious stand-up routines as well.
Two of our favorite children's shows on the app, that I recommend for ages 10 and up and their parents, are the Tuttle Twins and the Wingfeather Saga. We've enjoyed reading the books too; they are very well written.
Ultimately, I'm just thrilled with the awareness promoted by Angel Studios on subjects that are mostly ignored by the main stream media, which was achieved with the releasing of the movie The Sound of Freedom last year. It is one of the most successful independent films of all time.
The owners of Angel Studios are dedicated in creating light-centered content for children and adults. I just had to tell you about this in case you weren't aware of it before summer is over, while you still have some extra time to check it out with your family before school starts back up, and life becomes a little busier again.
~Be Well and God Bless You.
By Jennifer Wimmer

title: Noah Abbott Selected as Best Buddy Champion
author: Jennifer Wimmer
description: By: Jennifer Wimmer Noah Abbott (13), of Hawesville, was nominated recently to be a Best Buddy Champion of the Year. He has been speaking at schools and parent support groups about what life on the…
content:
By: Jennifer Wimmer
Noah Abbott (13), of Hawesville, was nominated recently to be a Best Buddy Champion of the Year. He has been speaking at schools and parent support groups about what life on the autism spectrum is like, and someone from the Best Buddies organization viewed one of his videos, and asked him to be an ambassador. He agreed, and completed his ambassador training with Program Manager Lee Anne Alsup, and she nominated Noah to be a 2024 Best Buddy Champion. He has a fundraising goal of $13K, and hopes to raise the most money for the Best Buddies organization, and win the competition.
The deadline for accepting donations is October 2nd, and the winner will be announced on October 3rd at the Best Buddy Gala in Louisville. Noah is also requesting donations of silent auction items. Any items that nominees bring for the silent auction at the Gala is added to the dollars they raise for the fundraiser.
'He is the youngest participant,' Noah's mom, Tiffany, said. 'I'm pretty sure he's the only Champion that has an intellectual development disability (IDD). He is trying to prove that he can do anything anybody else can do.'
To donate, please go to this direct link: https://www.bestbuddieschampion.org/kentucky/supporting/#noah. This is the organization's biggest fundraiser of the year. Best Buddies is an international program, and they are a sister organization to the Special Olympics.
Last week, Noah and his family traveled to Louisville for the Best Buddy Champion Training Day, and a fun Champion Kickoff Party.
'He did the training just to go over rules,' Tiffany said, 'and they gave him a lot of really good ideas on how to fundraise. At the Kickoff Party, they introduce them, and each Champion nominee is assigned a Mission Partner. The Mission Partners work with the Champions, and it's the Champion's responsibility to fundraise. It's an 8-week fundraising competition.'
The Mission Partner is someone who has an IDD that Best Buddies will support in all kinds of ways. A great way to help a Champion like Noah raise money is to help him get sponsorships for tables at the Gala. A table for 10 is $1,500, and that includes dinner, entertainment, and the silent and live auctions. Individual tickets to the Gala are also available for $150 per person. Because Noah is a Champion with an IDD, he is assigned a Campaign Manager, instead of a Mission Partner, and Tiffany will fill that role because he is the only participant in this area.
All of the nominees were allowed to bring up to 5 guests for the Kickoff Party last Thursday night. Noah and his parents attended, and they got to bring his friend, Carlee Page, and her mom, Jessica Page, as guests. Noah was elated to be there, and to be chosen as a Champion, as well as telling his community about the organization in The Hancock Clarion.
'I just wanted you (the readers) to get to know what Best Buddies is like,' Noah said. 'They have One-to-One Friendships. They'll go to elementary, middle, and high schools, and colleges, and even citizens can participate in this program. It helps create an inclusive community for these people to join, and for students and adults with IDD, and it helps them really become socially integrated with their peers, and it's for every age.
Because a lot of the IDD community is self isolated, this program can help them make friends. They have another one called E-Buddies. It's virtual, and helps them reach a wider range of people. They have Integrated Employment, which secures jobs for people with IDD. They help find their best skills, and it matches them up with the perfect job for them.
Then, they have Leadership Development. It is training for these people to help earn jobs at the Best Buddies organization itself. And, they have Best Buddies Ambassadors, which I did a training for. It offers people with and without IDD the opportunity to gain public speaking skills, self-esteem, and the confidence needed to successfully advocate for themselves, their peers, and Best Buddies communities and workplaces. They can use this if they want to become a speaker when they grow up.
There is Best Buddies Promoters that empowers youth to become advocates for people with IDD. I think Best Buddies Kentucky has 19 high school chapters, several elementary school chapters, and a few middle school chapters. They help promote the chapters in Best Buddies to bring awareness to the Disability Rights Movement.
They have Transitions, and that offers a combination classroom based training of experiential learning and corporate mentorship that helps students with IDD explore post-secondary options to prepare for independent living, and identify career ambitions. They also have Inclusive Living, which provides an integrated experience in which people with and without IDD are active, contributing citizens.
The program for families provides them with access to individual connections and community resources to assist them on their journey of supporting a family member with IDD. A lot of people with IDD, and families of people with IDD don't really know how to help them and they get scared sometimes. The Family Support Program helps with that.
Eunie's Buddies connects families who are expecting or who have a young child with IDD to experience parents of a child with IDD, encouraging a genuine relationship routed in mentorship, resource sharing, and guidance. Families that have had children with IDD or experience with that, they can go to families who have just found out that their child has an IDD, or have a young child with IDD, and they help guide that parent for the process of the wonders of having a child with IDD.'
Tiffany and Noah are currently trying to start a Best Buddy Chapter in Hancock County. The organization provides all of the training necessary, and all of the materials to the schools, free of charge, to help form friendships between children like Noah and neurotypical kids, Tiffany said.
Noah created his own website about 4 months ago, completely on his own. On his website, there is a video of one of his speaking presentations, and there are ways to donate to help him travel to those. The website also has his life story, and why he loves being a motivational speaker. He's adding to it as he continues on with his speaking presentations and fundraising missions. Visit his website at: www.noahabbott.org.
He has fulfilled speaking engagements such as at the HC Public Libraries for the Autism Advocates of Hancock County support group, and at Miss Candy's Kids for Autistic Children support group, a nonprofit organization in Perry County, Indiana, created in loving memory of Candy Boerste.
'He never ceases to amaze me,' Tiffany said. 'When Noah was diagnosed (at age 3) we were told he would never speak . . .and now he is a speaker!'
He volunteers at the Hancock County Animal Shelter, and hosted the Give-A-Dog-A-Ball Event in April of this year, which was his original idea that he pitched to Animal Shelter Director and County Dog Warden Ronnie York. Ronnie loved the idea and agreed, and they raised donations totaling $275. All of those dollars went to Shelter Supporters of Hancock County.
He loves to help his community in any way he can. When he was attending 4th grade at North Hancock, before he began homeschooling, he created a fundraising benefit for the Family Resource Center, and raised $2K. Commonwealth Rolled Products matched that, and $4K was given toward Christmas gifts for children. Noah types around 100 words per minute, and he organized this fundraiser as a fun typing event, where he challenged his teachers. They would pay $10 to challenge him. On social media, he also invited people from the community to challenge him and they did the same.
He has collected stuffed animals for the HC Courthouse to give to children who may be a little nervous while being in the courtroom. He has donated part of his profits from a lemonade stand to an individual in a neighboring county who was battling cancer as well.
Noah said that when he receives encouraging words that he has inspired people with his motivational speaking, or with the fundraisers he organizes, that it really makes him happy.
'It helps me know that I am really helping my community,' he said, 'and impacting the world one presentation at a time. Even something as small as giving a dollar to a homeless person; That's helping your community. You may not be able to help more of the world, but you know what, I don't care if you help one person or if you help a thousand, I'm just glad that you're helping people.'
Noah's parents, Josh & Tiffany Abbott, are celebrating 15 years of marriage in September. Josh is the Infrastructure (IT) Manager for Commonwealth Rolled Products, and the couple also work together on their laser engraving home business, Tiffany's Timeless Treasures (visit the FB Page for more details).
They are blessed with 5 children; four are adults now. Noah is their youngest, and will be 14 in December. He's starting 7th grade this school year, and is enjoying homeschool.
Best Buddies was founded in 1989 by Anthony K. Shriver. There are nearly 3,000 chapters worldwide, and their programs engage participants in all 50 states, and in 45 countries around the world. For more information about Best Buddies International, check out the website at: https://www.bestbuddies.org. On the website, you can also find information on Best Buddies Kentucky.

title: A Family Legacy Reborn: Blackford Creek Bakery to Open in Hawesville
author: Jennifer Wimmer
description: By Jennifer Wimmer The Grand Opening for Blackford Creek Bakery, in Hawesville, is Wednesday, October 16th. Look forward to enjoying fresh donuts, fresh bagels with a variety of cream cheese spreads…
content:
By Jennifer Wimmer
The Grand Opening for Blackford Creek Bakery, in Hawesville, is Wednesday, October 16th. Look forward to enjoying fresh donuts, fresh bagels with a variety of cream cheese spreads to choose from, fresh baked bread, delicious butter spreads, freshly made chicken salad and pimento cheese spread, and a daily assortment of cakes, pies and desserts!
Tarren Powers, is renewing a family tradition by opening this bakery. Her grandmother, the late Margaret Powers, owned the Kozy Kitchen in Hawesville for many years, and was known in the community for her homestyle and delicious pies and baked goods.
Tarren is a 2008 Hancock County High School graduate. She grew up in the Hawesville/Pellville area of the county, where Blackford Creek runs through, and learned everything she knows about baking old fashioned southern desserts from her Grandma Powers.
'She was very big on community involvement,' Tarren said. 'I'm really excited to be able to mimic her in that way by providing to my community, and be involved, and be a part of people's holidays and events. We live in such a fast-paced world. It seems like so many people don't have time to cook. I enjoy doing that, and it helps keep her memory alive for me. I'm excited to be able to provide pies, rolls, breads, and all of the good stuff for people to maybe take for their family for Thanksgiving, Christmas, birthdays, etc., and have a piece of my family that they can share with their family.'
She added, 'My grandma had the Kozy Kitchen, up by Bill's IGA. Her daughter, my mom, Leslie, opened the Little Kozy Kitchen in 2009, in this same building. She (Margaret) passed two years ago, and that was really hard. I would have loved for her to have been here to see this. Everyone talked about her pies. Those are her famous pies, and I will be making those starting in November for Thanksgiving.'
Tarren's brother, Daxton King, cooked and baked with their Grandma Powers as well, and he is her 'right hand man' at the bakery, she said. Her vision is to bring you the nostalgic memories of your mom, grandma, or great-grandma's cooking, mixed with her own influences and modern twists.
Tarren's business partner is Travis Neff. Travis and his wife, Brittany, own and run Half a Pond Homestead on their 4-acre farm in Hawesville, and homeschool their 2 children. They raise multiple gardens, as well as rabbits, quail, and chickens. They craft and sell Kentucky Rebel Scum Hot Sauces, which will be available for purchase at the bakery soon!
Pies
Tarren is featuring her grandmother's original recipes for 'Chess Bars', and her famous, old-fashioned chocolate and coconut cream pies, as well as classic pumpkin pie, apple pie, persimmon cheesecake, chess pie, pumpkin cheesecake, and Kentucky Rebel Scum (KRS) bourbon pecan pie will also be featured soon. The pies will be available for order beginning next month!
Cakes
Specialty cakes are available in 6-inch round, 8-inch round, 10-inch round, and other sizes. Some of the offerings will be: German chocolate, Italian cream, carrot, red velvet, classic yellow, chocolate, strawberry, French vanilla, and blueberry lemon. (*Advance notice is required for guaranteed pick-up, and limited amounts are available for take-out.)
Donuts
Fresh donut varieties will include: raspberry jelly filled, glazed, chocolate dipped glazed, blueberry cake, chocolate long johns (filled and unfilled), and donut holes. Rotational donuts to look forward to are 'Tiger Tails' and apple fritters! Other delicious treats offered include sticky buns and honey buns.
Tarren said she plans on making specialty donuts themed for new movie releases each month. Some will feature favorite children's movie characters, and others will be themed such as for the new Stranger Things season coming out next year, she said.
On the Fall Seasonal Menu are: apple pie, pumpkin pie, pecan pie, pumpkin roll, chocolate chip pumpkin bread, pecan apple cinnamon bread, bread pudding, and pumpkin snickerdoodle cookies.
Decaf & Regular Coffee
Enjoy any of these delicious menu options with a cup of fresh coffee, caffeinated or decaffeinated. There will be a house blend and a daily variety available to choose from. Bottled drinks are also available for purchase. Gluten-free, sugar-free & Keto options on your favorites are coming soon!
On the grand opening day, Tarren will be giving out coupons to her first visitors. She won't be taking custom orders for the opening day. The official Ribbon Cutting Ceremony will be scheduled for a later date.
Blackford Creek Bakery is located at 164 Main Cross Street in Downtown Hawesville. The hours of operation are: Wednesday-Friday, 5:30 a.m.-3:30 p.m., and Saturday & Sunday, 5:30 a.m.-noon. The phone number is (270) 927-4019, and the email address is: blackfordcreekbakery@yahoo.com. Check out the website at: https://blackfordcreekbakery.com. Like and follow the Blackford Creek Bakery Facebook Page!

title: Healthy Habits
description: Healthier Sodas We are at that time of year for seasonal get-togethers, and there are many options to replace the sugary sodas at the snack table with healthier ones that are just as tasty! I've been…
content:
Healthier Sodas
We are at that time of year for seasonal get-togethers, and there are many options to replace the sugary sodas at the snack table with healthier ones that are just as tasty!
I've been on a mission to find healthy sodas that are flavorful. It is a simple pleasure that I'm just not willing to give up! Here's what I've found, and I hope that it helps other 'soda addicts' like me to still be able to enjoy carbonated beverages that are a little healthier than the ones loaded with sugar, high-fructose corn syrup, and/or artificial flavors, colors, sweeteners, and preservatives.
Kombucha
I started out with making my own root beer by using the kombucha I was already making at home, and adding the traditional root beer herbs for flavoring during a second fermentation/flavoring. You can get the complete details on how to make it, and other kombucha/soda flavors by checking out my 2 columns on kombucha in the 11-10-2022 and 11-17-2022 editions of The Clarion.
Olipop
Kombucha-making is quite a process, and after years of making it, I needed a break but still wanted my root beer! So, I found Olipop Brand, sugar-free, prebiotic sodas. The root beer flavor is my favorite, but the other flavors are tasty as well, and they offer one for almost every taste you're looking for – a Sprite knock-off, Mt. Dew-type flavor, cherry cola, faux Dr. Pepper, etc.
Izze
Another great natural soda, only sweetened with fruit juice, is Izze Brand. This sparkling juice soda is available in many different flavors, including: pomegranate, cherry lime, mango, strawberry, and blackberry.
Fall Punch
I like using the clementine (orange) flavor Izze in place of Sprite or 7 Up to make punch, and it works great! The orange color makes it perfect for fall get-togethers. Izze is also a two-in-one, because it contains juice and sparkling water. You can make a 'dreamsicle' style punch by adding scoops of vanilla ice cream. So Delicious Brand vanilla, sugar-free, vegan ice cream is a great option for helping those attending your party who have lactose intolerance to be able to enjoy the punch, as well as those who have to watch their sugar intake.
Sparkling Water
I decided to purchase a sparkling water maker, and opted for the Philips Brand. It carbonates cold water (preferably, filtered spring water), and then you can add any flavor syrup you'd like! You can make your own syrups and sweeten them with organic maple syrup or local honey, for example. You do have to purchase the CO2 tanks separately but they can be refilled, and last for awhile. This machine does not require electricity, which is a bonus, and it was relatively inexpensive when you consider the cost-savings over time. Unfortunately, the natural soda varieties are pretty expensive, and making your own is the way to go.
For those of you who don't want to make your own syrups for adding to your homemade sparkling water, and are a root beer fan like me, Portland Syrups Brand 'Genuine Root Beer Syrup' is SO GOOD. It does have organic cane sugar and brown sugar as the second and third ingredients. So, it would not be the best choice for those with blood sugar challenges, but it is healthier than syrups sweetened with high-fructose corn syrup, and other unhealthy ingredients.
~Be Well and God Bless You.

title: 2024 Annual Cruisin The Park – This Saturday at Vastwood
author: Jennifer Wimmer
description: By Jennifer Wimmer The 2024 Annual 'Cruisin The Park' vintage car show is on Saturday, October 19th, at Vastwood Park from 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. It is the tenth year for this family-friendly car…
content:
By Jennifer Wimmer
The 2024 Annual 'Cruisin The Park' vintage car show is on Saturday, October 19th, at Vastwood Park from 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.
It is the tenth year for this family-friendly car show event, and all proceeds from t-shirt sales and the '50/50 Pot' will be given to young Raelan Hodges and her family, in support of her brave battle with leukemia.
This year's organizers are Tracy & Glenda Johnson, and Brian & Mandy Natier. Glenda's father, Tom Owens, loved old cars, and taught Tracy how to work on them. Tracy started collecting in the late 80's, and has some gems, such as a 1940 Chevy Coupe, a 1948 Chevy Sedan, a 1955 Chevy 1st Series Pickup Truck, a 1972 Chevy Pickup Truck, and a 1979 Ford Thunderbird.
Glenda & Tracy (a Hawesville City Councilman), along with other couples in the county, began organizing Cruisin The Park 10 years ago. It is usually scheduled for the 3rd Saturday of October each year, and participants from the county and surrounding areas have brought as many as 300 vintage cars to show, in past years.
Tracy said, 'One guy that usually is always there, he has a '29 model, and we'll have everything from there to – some people have brought '20 or '23 Corvettes. We've had anything from old to new. If you want to show it, you're welcome. We have some people from as far as Southern Illinois attend, and Indiana; People come from all over. They just cruise in and park, and people look at the cars. Registration is free. We don't do early registration; Register when you get there. Cash prizes will be drawn with the number you're given with registration.'
T-Shirts
Cruisin The Park T-Shirts will be on sale for $15, at the registration table set-up at the Vastwood Beach House.
Vintage Bike Display
Mark Stephens will be there this year displaying his bicycle collection at the tennis court.
'He has all types of bikes,' Tracy said. 'Schwinn bikes, old 'Evil Knievel' bikes, etc. He displayed those at the fundraiser at Roseville (Park), and someone asked him if he would bring them. It will be a display for the kids to look at. I think he has maybe one or two old custom motorcycles, but mostly bicycles.'
Children's Activities
'There will be activities for the kids. There will be a racetrack and Hot Wheels cars that they'll be able to race, and I think there will be some prizes for the kids with that,' Tracy said.
Food
Lewisport Baptist Church will have free coffee and donuts early in the morning at Vastwood for this event. The normal start time for the Cruise-In is 10 a.m., but people show up earlier, Tracy said. There will also be two food trucks this year: Sunny Daze and J's Good Grub. The Galaxy Restaurant is located at the Park, and offers pizza, barbecue, and many other foods to choose from as well.
Cruisin The Park is held at the 400-acre Vastwood Park every year, just in time to view the spectacular leaf colors. The Park is located at 925 Vastwood Park Road, in Hawesville. There are 2 entrances: One entrance is located off of Hwy 60, between the cities of Lewisport and Hawesville, and the other is at 925 Vastwood Park Rd.

title: Mack Shearn: Official Hornet
author: Chelsea Boling
description: By Chelsea Boling Football is a way of life in the Shearn household. For Hayden, Graham, and Mack Shearn, the sport isn't just a passion&#
content:
By Chelsea Boling
Football is a way of life in the Shearn household. For Hayden, Graham, and Mack Shearn, the sport isn't just a passion—it's a family legacy. As third-generation Hornets, football pulses through their veins. Hayden, wearing #1, is a senior while his younger brother Graham, #2, is a sophomore. And then there's Mack, their 8-year-old little brother, who may not be able to physically suit up, but holds a title that's just as important—Hornet Foot ball's number one fan.
Recently, Mack had the opportunity of a lifetime, thanks to Head Coach Bobby Eu banks. Mack was invited to serve as an honorary team captain at a Hornet Football game, joining his brothers and his father, Kirk Shearn, who serves as an assistant coach. As Mack proudly walked onto the field hand in hand with Hayden and Graham, alongside his dad, the crowd felt the magnitude of the moment.
What made this even more special is what Mack's mom shared with me. 'Mack will physically and mentally never be able to play sports, so it meant the world to us that he could experience being on the field with both of his brothers before Hayden graduates.' Mack was born with 3p Deletion Syndrome, a rare genetic disorder where part of the short arm of chromosome 3 is missing. This condition brings with it significant challenges, including intellectual disabilities, developmental delays, and physical symptoms such as con genital heart defects, seizure disorders, and low muscle tone.
Despite these hurdles, Mack's enthusiasm for the game remains unparalleled. His love for the Friday night lights rivals that of any athlete, and his presence in the stands is a source of pride for the Shearn family and the entire Hornet community. Mack may never don a helmet, but his role as the team's number one fan is vital, reminding us all how important fans are to the game. After all, what would sports be without the roar of the crowd? That exhilarating moment when a last-second touchdown is scored wouldn't be the same without the thunderous cheers of those watching.
We all have a part to play—on the field and off. While some roles may seem more import ant, they are all essential to the team's spirit. For Mack, his position in the Hornet family is just as meaningful as his brothers' on the field. His journey and his joy remind us of the strength in this community and the power of inclusion.
The Shearn family would like to extend their deepest gratitude to Coach Bobby Eubanks and the entire coaching staff for making this unforgettable moment possible, showing that true team spirit goes far beyond the game.

title: Wall and Wigginton Compete for District 1 Magistrate Seat
author: Jennifer Wimmer
content:
By Jennifer Wimmer
Hancock County voters will have one magistrate race on the ballot this year for District 1 (Lewisport). Darrell Wall (D), has been serving since May, and until the election, for John Garner (D), former Lewisport Chief of Police, who vacated the seat to serve as School Resource Officer at North Hancock Elementary. Chosen by the Hancock County Democrat Party, Wall was sworn-in as the interim Lewisport, District 1 Magistrate in April. His challenger, the candidate selected by the Hancock County Republican Party, is former Lewisport City Administrator Brent Wigginton.
Darrell will continue to hold the office, as the governor-appointed candidate, until a candidate is elected during the general election on November 5th, which is right around the corner. The newly elected individual will take office immediately and fill Garner's unexpired term.
Independent Candidates
As reported in The Clarion, the deadline for Independent candidates to submit their nomination forms was June 4th, 2024, per the filing deadline.
Write-In Candidates
Any qualified individual may run as a Write-In candidate as long as they file a declaration on intent in the Clerk's office by Friday, October 25th. Their name will not appear on the ballot. It will be up to the voter to write the candidate's name on the ballot next to the coordinating office. Only votes for candidates who have filed the proper write-in filing paperwork will be counted.
Brent Wigginton
Brent Wigginton served the City of Lewisport for 22 years. He was hired by the City in 2001 for the Public Works position as operator of gas, water and sewer, and for 16 years served as Lewisport City Administrator. He was also a volunteer firefighter at the Lewisport Volunteer Fire Department (LVFD) for many years.
He retired in 2022, but is still very active in the city. He continues to serve on many local committees and clubs, such as the Heritage Festival, Christmas in the Park, and the Lewisport Lions Club. Since 2010, he has been a Kenergy Board Representative for Hancock County, and is the current General Manager of Daviess County Water District.
Brent was involved for many years with the Hancock County Softball Rec. League, and for 14 years with the HC Softball Boosters, while his daughters were growing up. He has worked closely with the HC Parks and HC School system, and emphasized the importance of our parks, as well as their partnership with the school system.
'I am running for the position of Magistrate District 1 to have the opportunity to serve our citizens and county,' Brent said. 'I have devoted most of my life to service through my employment with the City of Lewisport, serving as a past member on the LVFD and the Lady Hornet Softball Boosters. I feel I bring many years of experience in communicating and working closely with local, state and federal governments. I have been tempered by having to navigate our way through snow and ice storms, wind storms and floods. I have extensive experience with fiscal budgeting and working side by side with our local agencies to fund projects such as infrastructure, roads, parks and public safety. During my career I have and presently still work with HC EMS, the HC Sheriff's Department, and county and state road departments. I serve our county as your Kenergy Board Representative and am very proud of the fact that our co-op is in the process of building fiber-based internet in our county; I have been able to be a part of that movement from its inception. We have a great county and I would love to have the opportunity to listen to your needs and do all in my power to help. There is a bright future for Hancock County and District 1. I believe through good governance and planning we can continue to have and create opportunity for our citizens, children and grandchildren.'
Brent is a 1988 HCHS Graduate. He and his wife, Renee, both county natives, are blessed with 2 daughters, Raelynn and Haley Ann. Raelynn and her husband, Russell Haycraft, have blessed them with 2 grandchildren, Collins Rae Haycraft and Micah Walker Haycraft.
Darrell Wall
Darrell Wall was born and raised in the county, and is an Electrician at Domtar in Hawesville. He and his wife, Donna, live on a farm in Lewisport that's been in her family since the early 1940s.
A 1982 HCHS Graduate, he earned his Associate's Degree in electronics in 1987 at Rets Electronic Institute, in Louisville, and has been working in industrial maintenance ever since. In addition to working at Domtar, he has also worked at Commonwealth (Martin Marietta at that time), the Big Rivers Coleman Station, and is a former small business owner.
Darrell has gained over 30 years of extensive knowledge on the inner workings of industry, and served as the President of the United Steel Workers Union in Hawesville, Local USW # 1261, from 2018-2024. His term ended earlier this year, which he said will free him up more to be dedicated in his service as District 1 Magistrate.
'I care a lot about the district and the people,' Darrell said. 'I will try to make myself readily available to the people. I still do work full-time at Domtar in Hawesville, but Hancock County is in my blood and I want to do the best I can to serve the constituents of that district in whatever is needed. I think oftentimes, and even in my past, I was quicker to speak instead of listening. I think listening goes a long way, especially in the position of a magistrate. You need to be able to listen to people, hear what they're saying and understand their needs. That's how I'll approach this position. I'm going to do my best to uphold their interests.'
He pledges to maintain a healthy fiscal budget; ensure proper roadway maintenance and care; adequately support our county employees, departments and programs; work on infrastructure upgrades, as needed, to best serve the citizens dependent on them; be available to deal with concerns within the district, and all of Hancock County; routinely travel and inspect district roads; and work with the HC Fiscal Court to provide best practice, and long-term plans.
Darrell & Donna are blessed with 3 children, Taylor, Rebecca and Anna. Rebecca and her husband, Zayne Boling, have blessed them with one grandson, Leyton Zayne Boling. While Taylor attended HCHS, he played basketball and football, and Darrell & Donna were very instrumental in helping with fundraisers and supporting the HC Hornets.

title: 2024 Ballot Breakdown
content:
There are several local races that will appear on the General Election ballot in Hancock County on Election Day, Tuesday, November 5th, in addition to the Kentucky Congressional contest, U.S. House of Representatives race, and the choice for President of the United States #47.
Questions on the Ballot
The ballot is lengthy this year, and will have a front and back. In addition to the races, there will be two constitutional amendments to vote 'yes' or 'no' on, as well as the question asking if you are in favor of the Kentucky Medical Marijuana Program and its implementation with local businesses being established in the county.
Succinctly, Amendment 1 asks voters if they want to ban voters who are non-citizens from voting in the Commonwealth of Kentucky. Amendment 2 asks voters if they want to allow lawmakers to allocate public tax dollars to other educational opportunities, such as charter or private schools.
Lewisport Mayor
For the City of Lewisport Mayor, Eddie Miller is challenging Lewisport Mayor Chad Gregory for the seat.
District 1 Magistrate
The race for the District 1 Magistrate seat is between Brent Wigginton and Darrell Wall.
City Council Members
Voters can select up to 6 candidates each to serve on the Lewisport City Council and Hawesville City Council.
Lewisport City Council
The six incumbents running for re-election to serve on the Lewisport City Council are: Marsha Johnson, Kelly Vanover, Josh Roberts, Tori Sipes Shively, Josephine 'Josie' Hagan, and Mary M. Hawkins. Roy White is also running for a seat on the council, and there is a Write-in option.
Hawesville City Council
Running for re-election to serve on the Hawesville City Council are incumbents Pat 'Junnie' Morris, Kevin Linn, Tracy O. Johnson, Justin Basham, Danny Doyle, and Wayne Herndon. Matt Patterson is running for a seat on the council as well, and there is a Write-in option.
Circuit Clerk
Hancock County Circuit Clerk Mike Boling is running unchallenged.
HC School Board
Veronica Taylor is challenging Donna M. Quattrocchi for the 2nd District Hancock County Board of Education (BOE) seat. Mary Beth Emmick Morris and Charles Todd Duncan are both running for the 5th District BOE seat. Incumbent Shane Ball is running, uncontested, for the 4th District BOE seat.
Commonwealth's Attorney
Blake Ross Chambers (R) is running unchallenged for election to the 38th Judicial Circuit Commonwealth's Attorney in Kentucky seat.
State Representative
Chanda Garner (D) is challenging incumbent Scott Lewis (R) to serve on the Kentucky House of Representatives, representing District 14.
U.S. Representative
Hank Linderman (D) is running for election against incumbent S. Brett Guthrie (R) for the United States House to represent Kentucky's 2nd Congressional District.
President and Vice President of the U.S.
Donald J. Trump and J.D. Vance are running on the Republican Party ticket. Kamala D. Harris and Tim Walz are running on the Democrat Party ticket. On the Kentucky Party ticket are Jill Stein and Samson LeBeau Kpadenou. The Independent Party candidates are: Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. and Nicole Shanahan, and Shiva Ayyadurai and Crystal Ellis. The Libertarian Party candidates are Chase Oliver and Mike ter Maat.
Deadlines
The deadline to request a mail-in absentee ballot was Tuesday, October 22nd. The six days of Excused In-Person Absentee Voting are: October 23rd, 24th, 25th, 28th, 29th, and 30th. No-Excuse In-Person Absentee 'Early' Voting begins on Thursday, October 31st and runs through Saturday, November 2nd. Traditional, in-person voting will be on Tuesday, November 5th.
Ballots may be returned by mail, or to the secure drop box located inside the Hancock County Clerk's Office, located at 225 Main Cross Street in Hawesville, during normal business hours of 8:00 a.m.-4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday. *Ballots must be received in the clerk's office by November 5th at 6:00 p.m.
Voting Precincts & Locations
Lewisport: West and East Lewisport Precincts (A101 & A102) will have a Consolidated Precinct Voting Location at the Lewisport Community Center to make it easier for voters. The Lewisport Community Center is located at 15 Pell Street in Lewisport.
Hawesville: West and East Hawesville Precincts (C101 & C102) will have a Consolidated Precinct Voting Location at the Hawesville Baptist Church New Life Center, located at 290 Main Street in Hawesville.
Yellow Creek: Precinct (B101) and All other Hancock County Precincts Voting Location is Hancock County High School, located at 80 St. Rt. 271 South in Hawesville.
Utility: Precinct (B102) and All other Hancock County Precincts Voting Location is North Hancock Elementary School, located at 330 Frank Luttrell Rd. in Lewisport.
Chambers: Precinct (B103) and All other Hancock County Precincts Voting Location is South Hancock Elementary School, located at 8631 St. Rt. 69 in Hawesville.
Indian Creek: Precinct (D101) Voting Location will be at Patesville Baptist Church, located at 3965 St. Rt. 144 in Hawesville.
Pellville: Precinct (D102) Voting Location will be at the Pellville Fire Station (South Hancock Volunteer Fire Department), located at 12194 St. Rt. 2181 in Hawesville.
Boling Chapel: Precinct (D103) Voting Location will be at Boling Chapel Church, located at 4435 Hawesville Easton Road.
*Lewisport Fire Station and Immaculate Conception Hall will not be used as precinct locations this election.
