title: New Leadership, Familiar Dedication: HC's Brandon Harley Becomes AACS CEO
author: Jennifer Wimmer
description: By Jennifer Wimmer Hancock County native Brandon Harley has recently been appointed as the new Chief Executive Officer of Audubon Area Community Services (A
content:
By Jennifer Wimmer Hancock County native Brandon Harley has recently been appointed as the new Chief Executive Officer of Audubon Area Community Services (AACS), in Owensboro. Brandon graduated from Hancock County High School in 1995, and is the son of Rick and Kim Harley, former owners of the Video Corner, in Hawesville. He worked at the business as a teenager, and also volunteered at Hancock County Audubon Area to earn his community service hours while attending HCHS. Kathy Elliott was the county coordinator at that time, and he worked with her on the weekends and after school. Rick and Kim are the former president and vice president of Hancock County Care & Share, and Brandon also worked with them in the community to help people in need. 'My philanthropic roots really began early-on in my life,' he said. 'I'd come in from college and help my parents with Care & Share, and over Christmas break they'd always do Christmas gift distribution at HCMS. We'd give out toys to the kids, we'd have a Santa Claus, a breakfast, and food distribution. That was really cool to be a part of back then.' He said those experiences sparked a passion in him for wanting to do more for the community, and helped to pave the road leading him to where he is today. Brandon earned his Bachelor's in Finance, Psychology and Sociology at Kentucky Wesleyan University, and a Master's Degree in Social Work at University of Louisville. He is a Board-Certified Social Worker with the Kentucky Board of Social Work. 'I always had an ambition to be a therapist and a counselor,' he said, 'but once I got my master's degree in 2005, I never practiced one day of therapy. Basically, people handed me spreadsheets, and I've been doing program management for the last 20+ years.' This is his second stint with AACS. His first job, out of college, was with the agency in 1999, and he worked with a small program called FIRST Project. 'We worked with kids who had undiagnosed mental health issues, and were interfacing with the juvenile justice system,' he said. 'I worked with families and kids, trying to get them hooked up with the services they needed, doing some case management planning with them, and trying to keep them out of juvenile detention and psychiatric placement, and really trying to get them on the right path.' He was in the position for almost a year, and worked closely with the Daviess County judicial system, the guidance offices and family resource coordinators in the school system, therapists at River Valley Behavioral Health, court designated workers, local judges, and the county prosecutor. In 2000, Brandon transferred into working with the Cabinet for Health and Family Services, and was a frontline social worker, with child protective, adult protective, and juvenile justice work for almost 15 years. He served as the regional administrator for the 17-county service region, overseeing all of those offices in the western part of the state. His second stint with AACS began in 2015, and has included his service as Deputy CEO and Chief Operating Officer. He's been continually committed to delivering support to low-income families and individuals through programs focused on such areas as senior services, recovery access to healthcare, and social support services, just to name a few. 'At its core,' Brandon said, 'Audubon Area is a community action agency. We're one of about a thousand community actions across the country. The ultimate goal of community action is to help people who are experiencing poverty, or with barriers that are keeping them in poverty, to live self-sufficiently. We do that by offering multiple services, whether that be building systems like LIHEAP (Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program), that we're running now in all of the counties, or through the head start centers, and our transportation network – GRITS (Green River Intra-county Transit System), and through our employment and housing services.' As the new AACS CEO, Brandon said his goal is to continue the mission of working in each one of the counties they serve to try to deliver as many of the services as possible to the residents in those communities. 'In Hancock County, Julie Newton is our County Coordinator and does an excellent job. I'm really proud of the work Julie does,' he said. 'We were classmates, and graduated together. I've known her all my life. She does a tremendous job interacting with the families, delivering the services, and being that resource, that point of contact, and that beacon of light in Hancock County. I want to offer more opportunities for her to deliver more services to all of our county. For instance, we don't have any housing units that Audubon operates in Hancock County, but I would be interested in trying to see if we could deliver more low-income, and affordable and safe housing opportunities in Hancock County in the years moving forward.' He said his long-term goal is to bring ALL of the AACS services to all of the counties they serve, and that local input is a key piece in how those services are delivered.
'Audubon is nothing without the partnerships,' he said. 'It's a big organization, and we have lots of services, but we would be nowhere without our board of directors. Chic (Judge-Executive Johnny Roberts) is on our board; I talk to him regularly. Mike Boling (HC Circuit Clerk) is also on the board. They are real advocates for the county citizens. They want to help Audubon, and help me deliver the best services we can. I really appreciate that local input.' The former AACS CEO, Rob Jones, will officially retire out of the position at the end of 2024. Brandon began as the organizational CEO, effective on November 16th, and Rob will be in an advisory role during the transition period.
Brandon and his wife, Sara, live in Owensboro. They are blessed with three children. Their oldest son, Clay (27), lives in Nashville. Their identical twin sons, Jacob and Nathan, are seniors at Daviess County High School. Audubon Area Community Services is the largest of 23 community action agencies serving residents of Kentucky. The agency is headquartered in Owensboro, and serves the primary 7-county Green River Area District, as well as Barren River, Cumberland, Pennyrile, Purchase, Lincoln Trail and Salt River area.
The Audubon Area mission is: 'Helping people in poverty and beyond to reach self-sufficiency by changing lives through providing services, advocacy, and partnering to strengthen communities throughout Kentucky.' Hancock County Audubon Area Community Services is located at 225 Main Cross Street, in Hawesville. The phone number is (270) 927-6500.

title: Help Baby Emilia: Donations Accepted at Parades and Fire Department Open House
content:
Donations for Local Firefighter's Family
Volunteer Firefighter with Dukes Volunteer Fire Department David Brandle, and his wife, Shelby Brandle, have been going through a very difficult time. Their newborn baby, Emilia Violet, suffered a stroke during birth, and has been in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit since then.
Emilia is making great strides. She is now off of her feeding tube and oxygen, and doing a lot better, but they still have a long way to go.
Donate at Parades
All of the county's fire departments will be collecting money, in addition to handing out candy at this year's parades in Hawesville and Lewisport. Donations will go directly to the Brandle family.
Donate at DVFD Open House
Dukes Volunteer Fire Department will also be collecting money during their Open House at the new fire station this Saturday, November 23rd, from noon to 4:00 p.m.
Donations can also be made at Bill's IGA and Hancock County Farm Supply.
'David and his family have shown up for this county for many years,' Director of HC Emergency Management and Volunteer Firefighter Kyle Veach said. 'I'd like for this county to show up for him in his time of need. It's a scary place for a young parent to be. There are a lot of unknowns. Even with the insurance, there is still fuel, travel expenses, meals, etc.'
Venmo
In addition to cash donations, a Venmo account will be set up in time for the parades, so that people can also scan the QR Code to donate via their cellphones. The Venmo account information will also be shared on all of the county's fire department Facebook pages soon, so that anyone can donate to help the Brandle family during their time of need.

title: Alwin John Ronald Meincken
description: Alwin John Ronald Meincken 96, of Lewisport passed on to his Heavenly Home on Tuesday November 12, 2024 at the Heartford House. Al was born on July 9, 1928 in East Providence, Rhode Island. He was a…
content:
Alwin John Ronald Meincken 96, of Lewisport passed on to his Heavenly Home on Tuesday November 12, 2024 at the Heartford House. Al was born on July 9, 1928 in East Providence, Rhode Island. He was a member of Hilldale Methodist Church where he was the technology manager for 29 years. He was an avid fisherman, a bird enthusiast, and knew every gadget available. Al retired from the US Army in 1966. He was a decorated Staff Sergeant, E6 and a WWII Veteran. Al was a 60 year member of the Masonic Lodge, a Scottish Rite Freemason, and a member of the Shriners. He was also bestowed the honor of Kentucky Colonel. In 1966 he received appointment as Honorable Deputy Sheriff and awarded Outstanding Contribution to Hancock County. Al devoted numerous hours to his community serving in many ways. He became involved in United Way as President in Hancock County, served as President of Hancock County Chamber of Commerce for two years, served on the Hancock County Planning and Zoning board for three years, and served on the Industrial Foundation as secretary for three years.
Survivors include his Wife Norma Meincken; a son John (Frieda) Meincken of Russell Springs, KY; grandchildren Brooke (Marcus) Bartrug of Russell Springs, KY, Alex (Jessica) Meincken of Mount Washington, KY, Nicholas Hollifield of Louisville, KY and seven great grandchildren. He was proceeded in death by his first wife, Isabella Lees Meincken. His father and mother, Harold and Winifred Meincken
A Memorial Service will be held at Noon, Friday, November 15, 2024 at Hilldale Methodist Church. Visitation will be from 11:00 am till the service time Friday at the church. Family request expressions of sympathy be made out to Hilldale Methodist Church. Share your memories and condolences for Al's family at www.gibsonandsonfh.com.

title: In Memory of Lesa Keown: Homemaker, Teacher, and Friend to All
author: Jennifer Wimmer
content:
By Jennifer Wimmer
Everyone in the Hancock County community, and all of us here at The Clarion were greatly saddened by the passing of Lesa Gail Patton Keown, of Hawesville, on January 5th. She was such a wonderful lady, and did so much to enrich the lives of others.
None of us were ready to let Lesa go so soon, and at such a young age. She was only 64-years-old, and was very active in the community. In her leadership roles, she contributed whole-heartedly to the adults, families, and the children in the community.
She was a Vision Center Optician at Wal-Mart Supercenter in Tell City for 37 years. When she wasn't working or volunteering her time to help others, she loved spending time with her grown children and grandchildren, and also going on adventures with Pam's Traveling Friends, of Lewisport.
Lesa was President of the Hancock County Homemaker Council, and President of the Hawesville Homemaker Club, as well as serving as the Green River Area Homemaker Vice President.
She wrote her column 'Homemaker Happenings' each week for The Hancock Clarion, keeping readers informed well in advance of events and classes. She was always encouraging people to get involved with the Homemakers, and with open arms to everyone.
She taught Sunday School at Hawesville Baptist Church, where she was a member for most of her life. And she served as the Blackford-Breckinridge Baptist Association's Woman's Missionary Union Director, in Hardinsburg. She was also a member of the Association's Missions Committee.
Lesa inspired everyone with her love of Christ Jesus, her dedication to missions, and her love of homemaking and teaching others. One of her favorite quotes, which she faithfully demonstrated, was: 'Be the change you want to see in the world,' a quote attributed to Mahatma Gandhi.
Lesa's passing happened so unexpectedly. Many are grieving this great loss of a loved one and true friend in the community. There are not words to adequately describe how heavy our hearts are during this time. We ask God to please comfort her family and close friends, especially, right now. Lesa, we will miss your smiling face! Rest in Peace, Dear One.
'Afterglow' By Helen Lowrie Marshall
I'd like the memory of me to be a happy one.
I'd like to leave an afterglow of smiles when life is done.
I'd like to leave an echo whispering softly down the ways,
Of happy times and laughing times and bright and sunny days.
I'd like the tears of those who grieve, to dry before the sun;
Of happy memories that I leave when life is done.

title: Lewisport Mayor Chad Gregory Speaks at Chamber Breakfast
description: In his speech at the Hancock County Chamber of Commerce Breakfast, Lewisport Mayor Chad Gregory announced that plans are solidifying for an upcoming town forum on the construction phase of the…
content: In his speech at the Hancock County Chamber of Commerce Breakfast, Lewisport Mayor Chad Gregory announced that plans are solidifying for an upcoming town forum on the construction phase of the regionalized water plant that will be built in Lewisport. Gregory was re-elected in November to serve a sixth term and said his main focus, for now, is the water plant. The town forum will be held at either Hancock County High School or North Hancock Elementary, he said, and will be open to the public. The date and time of the forum will be published in The Clarion as soon as those details are available. 'That town forum is going to explain why we're doing it, how we're going to do it, and how we're going to pay for it,' Gregory said. Currently, the city is in the very first phases of construction planning on the $15M water plant. $8M in grant funding has been awarded so far, which will be utilized for the construction phase. All of the plans with the goal to be achieved have been submitted. In that grant process, the city will have the ability to be forgiven approximately $6M of the $8M. Additional funding could potentially be awarded this year, as they are up in the ranks to be awarded those additional dollars. ' I want to get the remaining funds for the regional water plant, an estimated 8 million, in 2025,' Gregory said. 'We hope to begin the construction phase in the next couple years. In the upcoming new Fiscal Year of '25-'26, the citizens of Lewisport need to be aware that potential rate studies are in place for the possibility of rate increases in water, sewer and natural gas. Rising material costs, insurance costs, coupled with rising inflation, have cut into our cash flow significantly. Rest assured, the council and employees are diligently looking at where to cut costs, and are holding off on non-essential projects for the foreseeable future.' Gregory said he's fairly certain that they will receive more funding this year. The water plant will have the potential to service all of Hancock County. 'That is a service that will stay here in Hancock County,' he said. 'Nothing will be outsourced.' There is discussion about the water plant being a stand-alone plant for both Lewisport and Hawesville. With this regionalization discussion of a Hawesville interconnect, the project went from 101st to 2nd on the list for grant funding, and then to number one.
